families.title: Provider connections
families.overview:
A provider connection is a named, shared credential (provider, API key,
optional base URL) that many LLM profiles link to instead of carrying their own
key. Under Settings → LLM, below **Available Profiles**, a user lists
connections with their linked-model count, adds them, edits them (rename,
provider, base URL, key rotation with a blank key meaning "keep"), bulk-adds
linked profiles from a row's menu, and deletes them; the server refuses to
delete a connection that a profile or the active settings still reference.
families.entry:
- Sidebar settings gear (`backend-selector-settings-link`), then **LLM** in the settings navigation (`sidebar-settings-/settings/llm`); the section sits below **Available Profiles**.
- Direct URL `/settings/llm`.
- Command menu (`Control+k`/`Meta+k`, or `command-menu-trigger`): search `LLM`, choose **LLM profiles**. Searching `provider connection` finds nothing.
- **Add connection** (`add-provider-connection`) opens the create modal; each row's `...` (`provider-connection-menu-trigger`) opens **Bulk add** / **Edit** / **Delete**.
- Elsewhere (other families): Model Router's editor has its own **Add connection** (`meta-profile-add-provider-connection`, see F12); the LLM profile editor links a profile to a connection and **Add from provider connections** bulk-adds without a preselected connection (see F10).
families.given:
Preconditions:

- A fresh `control-openhands launch --new`, doctored, `onboard --skip` done, desktop viewport. Do not run `llm preset deepseek` before this family: the recipes need no LLM profile and no connection (`control-openhands api GET /api/profiles` lists none, `control-openhands api GET /api/llm/provider-connections` is `[]`), so the profile added in Bulk add becomes the active one.
- A DeepSeek key in a file (`<key file>`). Pass it only with `browser fill ... --value-file <key file>`; never on the command line.
- `F11.agent-uses-connection` and `F11.rotate` start three tiny conversations on `deepseek/deepseek-flash`.
- `F11.load-error` is arranged by making the run's own connections store unreadable (a shell arrange step that writes only `$OH_VERIFY_RUN/private/provider-connections/provider_connections.json`, restored afterwards); `service stop agent-server` does not work because it replaces the whole page with `agent-server-onboarding-screen`.
- Blocked here: `F11.cloud` (needs a Cloud account with and without an organization, as owner and as member).
families.gotchas:
- Select the Provider by clicking an option (`testid=provider-item-<name>` exists only for verified providers; use `'role=option[name="<label>"]'` for the others), or with `browser choose 'testid=provider-connection-provider-input' <label>`. `browser fill` alone types a filter that is cleared on blur and leaves Save disabled.
- `browser fill ... --value-file <key file>` needs no positional value and prints only the length; keep keys out of commands and screenshots (the field is a password input).
- Duplicate display names are accepted (two rows called `QA_conn`), and so is any base URL text; rows then differ only by order (`'testid=provider-connection-row >> nth=1'`). Keep fixture names unique.
- Edit's Save is enabled even with no changes, and a blank key on Edit is omitted from the request (the stored key is kept); there is no way to clear a key.
- The delete spinner (`aria-busy`) lasts under 100 ms on a local stack; `--observe` sees only `Delete` then `<absent>`.
- `role=dialog` matches two nested elements in these modals; count `> 0`, do not expect `1`.
- The first profile added on a run with no profiles becomes the active one. Activating a linked profile copies the resolved key into the active agent settings, which keep the connection id: that is why the server still counts a reference after every linked profile is gone (see `F11.delete-stale-reference`) ([OpenHands/software-agent-sdk#5498](https://github.com/OpenHands/software-agent-sdk/issues/5498)).
- Delete a connection's linked profiles before the connection; then also make an unlinked profile active, or the delete is refused.
- Rotation results are read from the conversation (`conversation events ... --kinds ConversationErrorEvent,MessageEvent` and the banner in the chat), not from the settings page, which never shows the key.
- Model Router's **Add connection** reuses this modal (F12); its toasts and fields are the same.
- `F11.load-error` needs a real server failure: the recipe corrupts this run's own `provider_connections.json` and restores it. Always restore it (keep the `.bak`), or every later family on the run sees the error; never touch another run's state.
- At phone width a long name squeezes the provider column to one letter (`d…`); the full values stay in the API and the name's `title`.
- Known issue [OpenHands/software-agent-sdk#5497](https://github.com/OpenHands/software-agent-sdk/issues/5497): after a key rotation, new conversations still run agent steps on the old key; only title generation uses the new one (`F11.rotate`).
- Known issue [OpenHands/software-agent-sdk#5207](https://github.com/OpenHands/software-agent-sdk/issues/5207): OpenRouter linked profiles can lose connection credentials at raw agent/condenser startup or reuse stale credentials after rotation; opaque reasoning can also be lost on persisted turns. End-to-end checks need an approved OpenRouter connection and a model returning reasoning_details, including the linked-profile switch and reload path; loopback failure does not prove them. (`F11.agent-uses-connection`, `F11.rotate`).

features.description: with no connections the section shows the heading `Provider connections`, the subline `Share one API key across multiple models.`, **Add connection** and `No provider connections yet. Add one to share an API key across models.`

each row shows the name, the provider, `<n> model(s)` (profiles linked to it), a green key-set icon and a `...` menu labelled `Provider connection menu`; the section is reachable from the settings nav, the command menu and the URL.

in **Add provider connection** focus starts on Name; Save stays disabled until Name, a picked Provider and API Key are non-blank (whitespace does not count); a provider typed but not picked is cleared; Enter does not submit.
the Provider combobox lists `Verified Models` (OpenHands, Anthropic, OpenAI, …, deepseek, …) and `Other Models` groups and filters as you type.
Save creates the connection (toast `Connection "<name>" created`); the row persists after a reload and a backend restart; the key is stored but never shown.
Cancel, Escape and a backdrop click close the modal without creating anything; reopening starts empty.
a server rejection (for example a name over 128 characters) keeps the modal open and toasts a readable message.
the `...` menu offers **Bulk add**, **Edit**, **Delete**; Escape, a click outside or a second trigger click close it; ArrowUp/ArrowDown move and wrap; Tab closes it.
opening the menu moves focus to its first item (**Bulk add**).

**Edit** opens `Edit provider connection` prefilled (key blank with placeholder `<hidden>` and hint `Leave blank to keep the current key.`); rename, provider and base URL changes persist (toast `Connection "<name>" updated`), a cleared base URL is stored as none, a blank name disables Save, and a rename shows in the linked profiles' group header.
**Bulk add** opens `Add models as profiles` with the row's provider and connection preselected; the profiles it adds are linked and the row's count goes up.
a conversation on a profile linked to the connection runs with the connection's key; an Edit with the key left blank keeps it working.
typing a new key rotates it for new conversations: an invalid key makes the next conversation fail with the provider's authentication error and no reply; rotating back restores replies.
**Delete** asks `Are you sure you want to delete the connection "<name>"?` (focus on Cancel); Cancel and Escape keep it; Delete removes it (toast `Connection "<name>" deleted`).
deleting a connection that profiles or the active settings reference is refused with the server's message naming them; the dialog stays open and the row stays.
once its last linked profile is deleted (row shows `0 model(s)`) the connection can be deleted, or the UI says how to clear the remaining reference.
at 390 px the rows, the row menu and the modals fit without horizontal overflow.

if listing connections fails (for example an unreadable connections store, `GET /api/llm/provider-connections` 400), the section shows `Failed to load provider connections.` (`provider-connections-load-error`) in red while the profiles list and **Add connection** still render.

a name at the 128-character limit is accepted; the row truncates the name and provider with an ellipsis, shows the full name as a hover tooltip (`title`) and keeps the `...` trigger in view at desktop and phone width.
a connection whose provider is not in the provider catalog (created through the API) opens in Edit with that provider preselected and listed under `Other Models`, and saving keeps it.
on Cloud the section appears only with an organization bound and for members allowed to manage profiles; local users always see it.

A provider typed but not picked is cleared: `control-openhands browser fill 'testid=provider-connection-provider-input' deepse`, `control-openhands browser click 'testid=provider-connection-name-input'`, then `browser value 'testid=provider-connection-provider-input'` is empty (pick deepseek again afterwards). The field shows the provider's label, not its id: picking `testid=provider-item-openai` makes `browser value 'testid=provider-connection-provider-input'` `OpenAI`. `control-openhands browser fill 'testid=provider-connection-provider-input' deep` narrows it to `deepseek` (verified) and `deepgram`, `DeepInfra`; then `control-openhands browser click 'testid=provider-item-deepseek'` and `control-openhands browser value 'testid=provider-connection-provider-input'` is `deepseek`. scenarios.name: F11--the-agent-uses-the-connection-s-key
scenarios.title: The agent uses the connection's key
scenarios.body: Open Edit on `QA_conn` (as above), leave the key blank, click `testid=provider-connection-submit` and `browser wait-text 'Connection "QA_conn" updated'`. Run `control-openhands conversation start --prompt "Reply with exactly the word: pong" --wait --timeout 180` (prints `<id>`, `"model": "deepseek/deepseek-flash"`, status `finished`), then `control-openhands conversation events <id> --kinds ConversationErrorEvent,MessageEvent`: the agent message is `pong` and there is no `ConversationErrorEvent`.
scenarios.raw: **The agent uses the connection's key (`F11.agent-uses-connection`).** Open Edit on `QA_conn` (as above), leave the key blank, click `testid=provider-connection-submit` and `browser wait-text 'Connection "QA_conn" updated'`. Run `control-openhands conversation start --prompt "Reply with exactly the word: pong" --wait --timeout 180` (prints `<id>`, `"model": "deepseek/deepseek-flash"`, status `finished`), then `control-openhands conversation events <id> --kinds ConversationErrorEvent,MessageEvent`: the agent message is `pong` and there is no `ConversationErrorEvent`.
expected: a conversation on a profile linked to the connection runs with the connection's key; an Edit with the key left blank keeps it working.
notes: Known issue [OpenHands/software-agent-sdk#5207](https://github.com/OpenHands/software-agent-sdk/issues/5207): OpenRouter linked profiles can lose connection credentials at raw agent/condenser startup or reuse stale credentials after rotation; opaque reasoning can also be lost on persisted turns. End-to-end checks need an approved OpenRouter connection and a model returning reasoning_details, including the linked-profile switch and reload path; loopback failure does not prove them. (`F11.agent-uses-connection`, `F11.rotate`).

scenarios.name: F11--rotate-the-key
scenarios.title: Rotate the key
scenarios.body: Run `control-openhands browser goto /settings/llm`, open Edit on `QA_conn`, `control-openhands browser fill 'testid=provider-connection-api-key-input' sk-qa-invalid-0000`, Save and `browser wait-text 'Connection "QA_conn" updated'`. Run `control-openhands conversation start --prompt "Reply with exactly the word: ping" --wait --timeout 180` and `control-openhands conversation events <id> --kinds ConversationErrorEvent,MessageEvent`. Expected: a `ConversationErrorEvent` and no agent reply. Today the conversation shows the banner `litellm.BadRequestError: DeepseekException - ... Authentication Fails, Your api key: ****0000 is invalid` (so the new key was used), yet the agent still answers `ping` in the same turn (fail, screenshot `--feature F11.rotate --name bad-key`). Rotate back: `browser goto /settings/llm`, Edit `QA_conn`, `control-openhands browser fill 'testid=provider-connection-api-key-input' --value-file <key file>`, Save; a new `conversation start --prompt "Reply with exactly the word: pong" --wait --timeout 180` has `pong` and no `ConversationErrorEvent`.
scenarios.raw: **Rotate the key (`F11.rotate`).** Run `control-openhands browser goto /settings/llm`, open Edit on `QA_conn`, `control-openhands browser fill 'testid=provider-connection-api-key-input' sk-qa-invalid-0000`, Save and `browser wait-text 'Connection "QA_conn" updated'`. Run `control-openhands conversation start --prompt "Reply with exactly the word: ping" --wait --timeout 180` and `control-openhands conversation events <id> --kinds ConversationErrorEvent,MessageEvent`. Expected: a `ConversationErrorEvent` and no agent reply. Today the conversation shows the banner `litellm.BadRequestError: DeepseekException - ... Authentication Fails, Your api key: ****0000 is invalid` (so the new key was used), yet the agent still answers `ping` in the same turn (fail, screenshot `--feature F11.rotate --name bad-key`). Rotate back: `browser goto /settings/llm`, Edit `QA_conn`, `control-openhands browser fill 'testid=provider-connection-api-key-input' --value-file <key file>`, Save; a new `conversation start --prompt "Reply with exactly the word: pong" --wait --timeout 180` has `pong` and no `ConversationErrorEvent`.
expected: typing a new key rotates it for new conversations: an invalid key makes the next conversation fail with the provider's authentication error and no reply; rotating back restores replies.
notes: Known issue [OpenHands/software-agent-sdk#5497](https://github.com/OpenHands/software-agent-sdk/issues/5497): after a key rotation, new conversations still run agent steps on the old key; only title generation uses the new one (`F11.rotate`).

Known issue [OpenHands/software-agent-sdk#5207](https://github.com/OpenHands/software-agent-sdk/issues/5207): OpenRouter linked profiles can lose connection credentials at raw agent/condenser startup or reuse stale credentials after rotation; opaque reasoning can also be lost on persisted turns. End-to-end checks need an approved OpenRouter connection and a model returning reasoning_details, including the linked-profile switch and reload path; loopback failure does not prove them. (`F11.agent-uses-connection`, `F11.rotate`).

scenarios.name: F11--delete-is-refused-while-referenced
scenarios.title: Delete is refused while referenced
scenarios.body: Run `control-openhands browser click 'testid=provider-connection-row >> has-text=QA_shared >> testid=provider-connection-menu-trigger'`, `control-openhands browser click 'testid=provider-connection-actions-menu >> testid=provider-connection-delete'`, `control-openhands browser click 'testid=delete-provider-connection-confirm'`, then `control-openhands browser toasts`: `Provider connection cannot be deleted while it is referenced by LLM profile(s): deepseek-flash and referenced by the active agent settings. Update those references before deleting it.` The dialog stays open (`browser count 'role=dialog'` > `0`); close it with `role=dialog >> role=button[name="Cancel"]`; after `browser reload` the row is still there.
scenarios.raw: **Delete is refused while referenced (`F11.delete-referenced`).** Run `control-openhands browser click 'testid=provider-connection-row >> has-text=QA_shared >> testid=provider-connection-menu-trigger'`, `control-openhands browser click 'testid=provider-connection-actions-menu >> testid=provider-connection-delete'`, `control-openhands browser click 'testid=delete-provider-connection-confirm'`, then `control-openhands browser toasts`: `Provider connection cannot be deleted while it is referenced by LLM profile(s): deepseek-flash and referenced by the active agent settings. Update those references before deleting it.` The dialog stays open (`browser count 'role=dialog'` > `0`); close it with `role=dialog >> role=button[name="Cancel"]`; after `browser reload` the row is still there.
expected: deleting a connection that profiles or the active settings reference is refused with the server's message naming them; the dialog stays open and the row stays.

scenarios.name: F11--delete
scenarios.title: Delete
scenarios.body: Run `control-openhands browser click 'testid=provider-connection-row >> has-text=QA_edited >> testid=provider-connection-menu-trigger'`, `control-openhands browser click 'testid=provider-connection-actions-menu >> testid=provider-connection-delete'` and `control-openhands browser snapshot 'role=dialog'`: `Delete provider connection`, `Are you sure you want to delete the connection "QA_edited"?`, buttons `Cancel` and `Delete`; `browser eval "document.activeElement.textContent"` is `Cancel` (screenshot `--feature F11.delete --name confirm`). `control-openhands browser click 'role=dialog >> role=button[name="Cancel"]'` keeps the row; reopen and `browser press Escape` keeps it too. Reopen, `control-openhands browser click 'testid=delete-provider-connection-confirm'`, `control-openhands browser wait-text 'Connection "QA_edited" deleted'`, `browser reload`: `browser count 'testid=provider-connection-row >> has-text=QA_edited'` is `0`.
scenarios.raw: **Delete (`F11.delete`).** Run `control-openhands browser click 'testid=provider-connection-row >> has-text=QA_edited >> testid=provider-connection-menu-trigger'`, `control-openhands browser click 'testid=provider-connection-actions-menu >> testid=provider-connection-delete'` and `control-openhands browser snapshot 'role=dialog'`: `Delete provider connection`, `Are you sure you want to delete the connection "QA_edited"?`, buttons `Cancel` and `Delete`; `browser eval "document.activeElement.textContent"` is `Cancel` (screenshot `--feature F11.delete --name confirm`). `control-openhands browser click 'role=dialog >> role=button[name="Cancel"]'` keeps the row; reopen and `browser press Escape` keeps it too. Reopen, `control-openhands browser click 'testid=delete-provider-connection-confirm'`, `control-openhands browser wait-text 'Connection "QA_edited" deleted'`, `browser reload`: `browser count 'testid=provider-connection-row >> has-text=QA_edited'` is `0`.
expected: **Delete** asks `Are you sure you want to delete the connection "<name>"?` (focus on Cancel); Cancel and Escape keep it; Delete removes it (toast `Connection "<name>" deleted`).

scenarios.name: F11--long-name-and-provider-change

At `browser viewport phone` after `browser scroll 'testid=add-provider-connection'`, `browser bbox 'testid=provider-connection-row >> has-text=QA_long >> testid=provider-connection-menu-trigger'` is inside the viewport with no horizontal overflow (screenshot `--name phone`); back to `browser viewport desktop`. Open Edit on `QA_long`: `browser count 'testid=provider-connection-modal >> testid=set-indicator'` is `1` (green key-set check beside API Key). `control-openhands browser choose 'testid=provider-connection-provider-input' Anthropic`, Save, `browser wait 'testid=provider-connection-modal' --state detached`, `browser reload`: the row reads `QA_long…\nanthropic\n0 model(s)` and `api GET /api/llm/provider-connections` shows `"provider": "anthropic"`.
scenarios.raw: **Long name and provider change (`F11.long-name`, `F11.edit`).** Create a connection named `"QA_long$(printf 'x%.0s' $(seq 1 121))"` (128 characters) with deepseek and `dummy-key-5` as above: toast `Connection "QA_long…" created`, modal closed. `control-openhands browser tooltip 'testid=provider-connection-row >> has-text=QA_long >> span[title]'` returns the full 128-character name (`source` `title attribute`), `browser eval` on that span shows `scrollWidth > clientWidth` with `text-overflow: ellipsis`, and `browser bbox 'testid=provider-connection-row >> has-text=QA_long'` is `insideViewport` `true`, `pageHorizontalOverflow` `false` (screenshot `--feature F11.long-name --name row`). At `browser viewport phone` after `browser scroll 'testid=add-provider-connection'`, `browser bbox 'testid=provider-connection-row >> has-text=QA_long >> testid=provider-connection-menu-trigger'` is inside the viewport with no horizontal overflow (screenshot `--name phone`); back to `browser viewport desktop`. Open Edit on `QA_long`: `browser count 'testid=provider-connection-modal >> testid=set-indicator'` is `1` (green key-set check beside API Key). `control-openhands browser choose 'testid=provider-connection-provider-input' Anthropic`, Save, `browser wait 'testid=provider-connection-modal' --state detached`, `browser reload`: the row reads `QA_long…\nanthropic\n0 model(s)` and `api GET /api/llm/provider-connections` shows `"provider": "anthropic"`.
expected: a name at the 128-character limit is accepted; the row truncates the name and provider with an ellipsis, shows the full name as a hover tooltip (`title`) and keeps the `...` trigger in view at desktop and phone width.

**Edit** opens `Edit provider connection` prefilled (key blank with placeholder `<hidden>` and hint `Leave blank to keep the current key.`); rename, provider and base URL changes persist (toast `Connection "<name>" updated`), a cleared base URL is stored as none, a blank name disables Save, and a rename shows in the linked profiles' group header.

scenarios.raw: **Persistence across a backend restart (`F11.create`).** Run `control-openhands restart` and `control-openhands browser reload`; `browser eval "[...document.querySelectorAll('[data-testid=provider-connection-row]')].map(r=>r.innerText.replace(/\n/g,'|')).join(' ; ')"` lists the same rows and counts as before (for example `QA_shared|deepseek|1 model(s) ; QA_long…|anthropic|0 model(s)`).
expected: Save creates the connection (toast `Connection "<name>" created`); the row persists after a reload and a backend restart; the key is stored but never shown.

scenarios.name: F11--load-error
scenarios.title: Load error
scenarios.body: With the baseline restored (connections `[]`), run the shell arrange step (it writes only this run's state; the file exists only once the run has created a connection, as the bullets above do, so on a run that never created one `cp` fails: create and delete one through **Add connection** first) `F=$OH_VERIFY_RUN/private/provider-connections/provider_connections.json; cp $F $F.bak; printf '{not json' > $F`. `control-openhands api GET /api/llm/provider-connections` is now `400` (`Provider connections file is unreadable: ...`) while `api GET /api/profiles` is `200`. Run `control-openhands browser reload`, `control-openhands browser text 'testid=provider-connections-load-error'` (`Failed to load provider connections.`), `browser count 'testid=add-provider-connection'` (`1`) and `browser count 'testid=profile-row'` (> `0`; screenshot `--feature F11.load-error --name error`). The message uses the theme's error colour (`browser eval "getComputedStyle(document.querySelector('[data-testid=provider-connections-load-error] p')).color"`: `rgb(231, 106, 94)` on OpenHands-Neutral, `rgb(192, 40, 45)` on Light+, #18330). The profile rows render only because no profile links to a connection at this point: with a linked profile `GET /api/profiles` fails with the same `400` and the list above shows `Failed to load profiles` instead (`F10.list-states`). Restore with `cp $F.bak $F && rm $F.bak`, `browser reload`: `testid=provider-connections-empty` is back and `provider-connections-load-error` count is `0`.
scenarios.raw: **Load error (`F11.load-error`).** With the baseline restored (connections `[]`), run the shell arrange step (it writes only this run's state; the file exists only once the run has created a connection, as the bullets above do, so on a run that never created one `cp` fails: create and delete one through **Add connection** first) `F=$OH_VERIFY_RUN/private/provider-connections/provider_connections.json; cp $F $F.bak; printf '{not json' > $F`. `control-openhands api GET /api/llm/provider-connections` is now `400` (`Provider connections file is unreadable: ...`) while `api GET /api/profiles` is `200`. Run `control-openhands browser reload`, `control-openhands browser text 'testid=provider-connections-load-error'` (`Failed to load provider connections.`), `browser count 'testid=add-provider-connection'` (`1`) and `browser count 'testid=profile-row'` (> `0`; screenshot `--feature F11.load-error --name error`). The message uses the theme's error colour (`browser eval "getComputedStyle(document.querySelector('[data-testid=provider-connections-load-error] p')).color"`: `rgb(231, 106, 94)` on OpenHands-Neutral, `rgb(192, 40, 45)` on Light+, #18330). The profile rows render only because no profile links to a connection at this point: with a linked profile `GET /api/profiles` fails with the same `400` and the list above shows `Failed to load profiles` instead (`F10.list-states`). Restore with `cp $F.bak $F && rm $F.bak`, `browser reload`: `testid=provider-connections-empty` is back and `provider-connections-load-error` count is `0`.
expected: if listing connections fails (for example an unreadable connections store, `GET /api/llm/provider-connections` 400), the section shows `Failed to load provider connections.` (`provider-connections-load-error`) in red while the profiles list and **Add connection** still render.

scenarios.name: F11--redacted-key-is-rejected
scenarios.title: Redacted key is rejected
scenarios.body: Add `QA_SENTINEL`, choose OpenAI, fill the API Key with the literal `**********` and Base URL with `http://127.0.0.1:1/v1`. Use the native keyboard Save (`browser focus 'testid=provider-connection-submit'`, `browser press Space`; the provider listbox can intercept pointer clicks). Read `api GET /api/llm/provider-connections --pick 0.api_key_set`. Expected: reject the placeholder. Known failure, reproduced 2026-10-12 ([OpenHands/software-agent-sdk#5624](https://github.com/OpenHands/software-agent-sdk/issues/5624)): creation succeeds with `api_key_set: false`. Editing that row, typing the same placeholder and keyboard-saving succeeds and changes it to `true`. A second create under `QA_SENTINEL_2` again succeeds with the key unset. The UI already prevents a whitespace-only key; this recipe drives the sentinel branch, not provider authentication. Remove both unreferenced fixture connections afterwards.

scenarios.name: F11--store-lock-keeps-unrelated-routes-responsive
scenarios.title: Store lock keeps unrelated routes responsive
scenarios.body: Hold only the own `private/provider-connections/.provider-connections.lock` from an external run-owned process using `fcntl.flock(..., LOCK_EX)` for 34 seconds. Start an authenticated provider-connections list request, then request the own Agent Server's `/alive` two seconds later; reload the actual LLM page and capture its stalled loading state. Expected: `/alive` answers within two seconds while the store request waits. Known failure, reproduced twice 2026-10-12 ([OpenHands/software-agent-sdk#5632](https://github.com/OpenHands/software-agent-sdk/issues/5632)): `/alive` returned 200 after 25.416 and 28.060 seconds. A direct request with a 45-second client deadline received the store's 503 after 30.052 seconds; the CLI's shorter request instead timed out. Release/close the own lock and run `doctor`; do not hold or alter any other run's stores.
scenarios.raw: **Store lock keeps unrelated routes responsive (`F11.list`).** Hold only the own `private/provider-connections/.provider-connections.lock` from an external run-owned process using `fcntl.flock(..., LOCK_EX)` for 34 seconds. A direct request with a 45-second client deadline received the store's 503 after 30.052 seconds; the CLI's shorter request instead timed out. Release/close the own lock and run `doctor`; do not hold or alter any other run's stores.
expected: each row shows the name, the provider, `<n> model(s)` (profiles linked to it), a green key-set icon and a `...` menu labelled `Provider connection menu`; the section is reachable from the settings nav, the command menu and the URL.

scenarios.name: F11--connection-url-edit-reaches-next-chat
scenarios.title: Connection URL edit reaches next chat
scenarios.body: Arrange a disposable OpenAI connection `QA_URL_PATCH` with a dummy key and `http://127.0.0.1:1/v1`, plus an activated linked `QA_URL_LINKED` profile without inline key/Base URL. From `/settings/llm`, open the exact connection row menu > `provider-connection-edit`, change `provider-connection-base-url-input` to `http://127.0.0.1:1/v2` and submit; `api GET /api/llm/provider-connections` confirms the stored URL. Start a fresh Home chat with a bounded no-tools prompt, then read only `agent.llm.base_url` in its run-owned `base_state.json`. Repeat the real edit to `/v3` and start another chat. Expected: each new runtime uses the newly saved URL. Known failure, reproduced twice 2026-10-12 ([#17803](https://github.com/OpenHands/OpenHands/issues/17803)): the connection persisted `/v2` and `/v3`, but settings and both new runtimes retained the activated `/v1` snapshot. All model endpoints refuse on loopback; no provider success is needed to observe resolution. Restore the neutral active profile, then delete only the own linked profile and connection.
scenarios.raw: **Connection URL edit reaches next chat (`F11.edit`, `F11.agent-uses-connection`).** Arrange a disposable OpenAI connection `QA_URL_PATCH` with a dummy key and `http://127.0.0.1:1/v1`, plus an activated linked `QA_URL_LINKED` profile without inline key/Base URL. From `/settings/llm`, open the exact connection row menu > `provider-connection-edit`, change `provider-connection-base-url-input` to `http://127.0.0.1:1/v2` and submit; `api GET /api/llm/provider-connections` confirms the stored URL. Start a fresh Home chat with a bounded no-tools prompt, then read only `agent.llm.base_url` in its run-owned `base_state.json`. Repeat the real edit to `/v3` and start another chat. Expected: each new runtime uses the newly saved URL. Known failure, reproduced twice 2026-10-12 ([#17803](https://github.com/OpenHands/OpenHands/issues/17803)): the connection persisted `/v2` and `/v3`, but settings and both new runtimes retained the activated `/v1` snapshot. All model endpoints refuse on loopback; no provider success is needed to observe resolution. Restore the neutral active profile, then delete only the own linked profile and connection.
expected: **Edit** opens `Edit provider connection` prefilled (key blank with placeholder `<hidden>` and hint `Leave blank to keep the current key.`); rename, provider and base URL changes persist (toast `Connection "<name>" updated`), a cleared base URL is stored as none, a blank name disables Save, and a rename shows in the linked profiles' group header.
a conversation on a profile linked to the connection runs with the connection's key; an Edit with the key left blank keeps it working.
notes: Known issue [OpenHands/software-agent-sdk#5207](https://github.com/OpenHands/software-agent-sdk/issues/5207): OpenRouter linked profiles can lose connection credentials at raw agent/condenser startup or reuse stale credentials after rotation; opaque reasoning can also be lost on persisted turns. End-to-end checks need an approved OpenRouter connection and a model returning reasoning_details, including the linked-profile switch and reload path; loopback failure does not prove them. (`F11.agent-uses-connection`, `F11.rotate`).
annotations: Known failure, reproduced twice 2026-10-12 ([#17803](https://github.com/OpenHands/OpenHands/issues/17803)): the connection persisted `/v2` and `/v3`, but settings and both new runtimes retained the activated `/v1` snapshot. All model endpoints refuse on loopback; no provider success is needed to observe resolution. Restore the neutral active profile, then delete only the own linked profile and connection.

families.title: Model router (meta-LLM profiles)
families.overview:
A model router (the UI also calls it a "meta-profile") names a classifier LLM
profile, a prompt template and a model table. While a router is active, every
new conversation gets a `route_task_to_model` tool: the classifier picks one
saved LLM profile from the table and the agent switches to it (the chat shows
`Switched to profile <name>`). With **Run on first message** on, the agent is
told to route the first user message before doing anything else. Users create
routers from the Router Pro / Router Flash templates or from scratch, can have
the missing router LLM profiles created from a provider connection, and
activate, edit and delete routers under Settings → Model Router.
families.entry:
- Sidebar settings gear (`backend-selector-settings-link`), then **Model Router** in the settings navigation (`sidebar-settings-/settings/meta-llm`, between LLM and Condenser). Used by `F12.page`.
- Direct URL `/settings/meta-llm`. Used by most recipes (`browser goto`).
- Command menu (`Control+k` or `Meta+k`, or `command-menu-trigger` in the sidebar): search "Model Router" (or "router", "meta"), choose **Model Router** ("Meta-profiles that route each task to the right LLM profile."). Used by `F12.page`.
- Per-router actions: the row `...` button (`meta-profile-menu-trigger-<name>`), then Edit / Set active / Delete.
- The effect of a router is seen in a conversation started from the home composer (`F12.route-first-message`; see F05/F06 for the composer and activity rendering).
families.given:
Preconditions:

- `F12.empty-states` needs a fresh `launch --new` with `onboard --skip` done and **before** `llm preset deepseek` (no LLM profiles, no routers).
- Everything after it needs `control-openhands llm preset deepseek --api-key-file <key file>` (profiles `deepseek-flash` and `deepseek-pro`), no meta-profile named `QA_*` (`control-openhands api GET /api/meta-profiles`), no provider connection (`control-openhands api GET /api/llm/provider-connections` is `[]`) and no LLM profile named `deepseek-chat` (`control-openhands api GET /api/profiles`).
- `F12.add-connection` and `F12.route-first-message` use the DeepSeek key file; never print it.
- Blocked here: `F12.unsupported` (needs an agent server older than software-agent-sdk #3744, for example `launch --new --sdk-ref <older release>`), `F12.cloud` (needs a Cloud account, with and without an organization) and `F12.load-error` (needs `/api/meta-profiles` to fail while the rest of the agent server answers; `service stop agent-server` swaps the whole app for the Manage backends card instead).
- Desktop viewport unless a bullet says otherwise.
families.gotchas:
- Settings nav test ids embed the route: quote `'testid=sidebar-settings-/settings/meta-llm'` as written.
- The empty-state hint about LLM profiles only exists before any profile is saved: drive `F12.empty-states` first on a fresh run.
- The first router you create is activated and turns **Run on first message** on by itself; later routers do neither. Any recipe that creates a router on an empty list changes both.
- `Run on first message` is an `sr-only` checkbox (keyboard reachable): click the label text inside `testid=meta-profile-run-at-conversation-start` and read `.checked`/`.disabled` with `browser eval`. The stored preference (`misc_settings.app_preferences.run_router_at_conversation_start`) is independent of what the disabled switch shows; with no active router it may still be `true`. Turn it off before deleting the last router, or a later "first router" will not re-enable it because it is already on.
- Router templates name 11 models (`gpt-5.4` … `claude-sonnet-4-5`) that will not exist in a sandbox. With a provider connection present, a template preselects it, and saving creates all 11 as LLM profiles linked to that connection unless you pick **Don't create profiles** first (`F12.create-more` does). If a run created them, remove them with `for p in gpt-5.4 gpt-5.5 minimax-m3 claude-opus-4-6 claude-opus-4-7 claude-opus-4-8 claude-fable-5 kimi-k2.5 kimi-k2.6 deepseek-v3.2-reasoner claude-sonnet-4-5; do control-openhands api DELETE /api/profiles/$p --write; done` (they live in the run's private state and only add rows to Settings → LLM).
- Profile matching is case-insensitive and exact by name: table rows are `- <profile name>: description`; existing `deepseek-flash`/`deepseek-pro` are not re-created, and the endpoint is derived as `<provider lowercased>/<name>`.
- The classifier and the model table refer to LLM *profile names*, not model ids. A router whose classifier profile does not exist (for example a template's `minimax-m3` without a connection) saves fine and only fails when a conversation tries to route.
- The agent decides whether to call `route_task_to_model`: a prompt that conflicts with routing (`Reply with only the word pong.`) made deepseek-flash skip the call even with the instruction present. Use a task-like prompt for the positive check and assert the system prompt via `events/search` for the instruction itself.
- `conversation events` does not print the system prompt; read it with `control-openhands api GET "/api/conversations/<id>/events/search?limit=1" --max-bytes 200000` and grep the output.
- `service stop agent-server` does not show this page's error state: the whole app switches to the Manage backends card (F02). Run `control-openhands restart` afterwards.
- The selection in the classifier and connection pickers is a combobox: open it with a click on the input, then click `role=option[name="..."]`; `browser fill` on the classifier sets a free-text value (allowed) instead of picking a profile.
- At 390 px the row truncates the name (`QA_route…`) and summary; read names with `browser text`, not the screenshot.
- The Model table placeholder displays separate lines (`F12.template-custom`).
- Known issue [OpenHands/software-agent-sdk#5878](https://github.com/OpenHands/software-agent-sdk/issues/5878): Router files can be written under a literal `~` directory when Agent Server was configured with leading-tilde `OH_PERSISTENCE_DIR`. Blocked on the normal absolute-path launcher fixture: needs a disposable server with private HOME/cwd and literal `~/...` or relative persistence configuration, then a router save and filesystem readback. Never point it at user state. (`F12.create-first`, `F12.list`).

features.description: Settings → **Model Router** opens `/settings/meta-llm` with the subtitle `Meta-profiles that route each task to the right LLM profile.`; the command menu offers a **Model Router** command that opens it, like the other settings pages.

with no LLM profiles the page says `Create LLM profiles first — meta-profiles route between your saved LLM profiles.`; with no routers it says `No meta-profiles yet. Add one to route tasks across your LLM profiles.` and **Run on first message** is off and disabled.
when only the meta-profile request fails, a red generic error shows under the header.
an agent server without `/api/meta-profiles` (404) shows `This backend doesn't support model routing yet. Update the agent server to manage meta-profiles.`
a Cloud backend without an organization shows `Meta-profiles are only available for local backends.`; an organization-bound Cloud backend shows the full page.

**Add Model Router** opens `Choose Model Router template` (Add OpenHands Router Pro, Add OpenHands Router Flash, Custom, Cancel); Cancel, Escape and a backdrop click close it; Pro and Flash prefill the name, classifier `minimax-m3`, their own long routing prompt and the same 11-model table.
**Custom** opens a blank editor; the placeholders show an example prompt and a two-line example model table.
Save stays disabled until the name is valid, a classifier is set and the prompt contains `{{ instance_text }}` (spaces inside the braces optional).
a new router cannot take an existing router's name (`A meta-profile with this name already exists...`, Save disabled).
**Add connection** in the create editor opens `Add provider connection`; saving it selects the new connection in the picker.
**Cancel** in `Add provider connection` closes it without creating a connection and keeps the editor's values and picker choice.
while the create or edit editor is open it replaces the list, **Add Model Router** and the switch; **Cancel** returns to the list without saving anything.

with a connection picked under **Create missing router LLM profiles using**, Save creates an LLM profile `<provider>/<name>` linked to that connection for every model-table name (and the classifier) that does not exist yet; **Don't create profiles** creates none.
saving the first router lists it, makes it Active and turns **Run on first message** on.
saving another router lists it and leaves the Active badge where it was.
each row shows the name, `<classifier> · Direct prompt`, an **Active** badge on the active router and a `...` menu; routers and the active choice survive a stack restart.
the row menu offers Edit, Set active (disabled on the active row) and Delete, and closes on Escape.
**Set active** toasts `Meta-profile "<name>" activated` and moves the badge.
**Edit** opens `Edit meta-profile` with the name locked and no connection picker; changes persist.
**Delete** asks `Are you sure you want to delete "<name>"? This cannot be undone.`; Cancel keeps the row, Delete removes it.
deleting the active router leaves no router active; the switch shows off and disabled, and new conversations get neither the tool nor the first-message instruction.
the switch saves immediately (no Save button, no toast) and survives a reload.

with a router active and the switch on, a new conversation routes its first message (`route_task_to_model` action, `Switched to profile <name>` in the chat); with the switch off the tool is still attached but the instruction is absent.
in a light colour theme the list heading and router names are readable.
the list, template modal, editor and row menu fit a 390 px viewport without horizontal overflow.

scenarios.body: On the fresh run run `control-openhands browser goto /settings/meta-llm`, `control-openhands browser text 'testid=meta-profile-no-llm-profiles'`, `control-openhands browser text 'testid=meta-profile-empty'` and `control-openhands browser eval "(()=>{const i=document.querySelector('[data-testid=meta-profile-run-at-conversation-start-switch]');return {checked:i.checked,disabled:i.disabled}})()"`. scenarios.name: F12--template-chooser

scenarios.body: Run `control-openhands browser click 'testid=add-meta-profile'` and `control-openhands browser snapshot 'role=dialog'`: dialog `Choose Model Router template` with buttons `Add OpenHands Router Pro`, `Add OpenHands Router Flash`, `Custom`, `Cancel`. `control-openhands browser click 'testid=meta-profile-template-cancel'` then `control-openhands browser count 'testid=meta-profile-template-modal'` is `0`; reopen and `control-openhands browser press Escape` gives `0` too. Reopen, `control-openhands browser click 'testid=meta-profile-template-router-pro'`, then `control-openhands browser value 'testid=meta-profile-name-input'` (`openhands-router-pro`), `control-openhands browser value 'testid=meta-profile-classifier-input'` (`minimax-m3`), `control-openhands browser eval "document.querySelector('[data-testid=meta-profile-model-table]').value.split('\n').length"` (`11`), `control-openhands browser eval "document.querySelector('[data-testid=meta-profile-prompt-template]').value.includes('{{ instance_text }}')"` (`true`), `control-openhands browser value 'testid=meta-profile-router-connection'` (`Don't create profiles` while no connection exists) and `control-openhands browser enabled 'testid=meta-profile-save'` (`true`). Leave with `control-openhands browser click 'testid=meta-profile-cancel'`. The Flash template (`testid=meta-profile-template-router-flash`) gives `openhands-router-flash`, the same classifier and identical table, and a different prompt (about 5,900 characters against Pro's 5,000; compare with `browser eval "document.querySelector('[data-testid=meta-profile-prompt-template]').value.length"`). Blocked on the normal absolute-path launcher fixture: needs a disposable server with private HOME/cwd and literal `~/...` or relative persistence configuration, then a router save and filesystem readback. Never point it at user state. (`F12.create-first`, `F12.list`).

scenarios.name: F12--routing-in-a-conversation
scenarios.title: Routing in a conversation
scenarios.body: Make `QA_router` active (row menu → Set active, `wait-text 'Meta-profile "QA_router" activated'`) with the switch on. Run `control-openhands conversation start --prompt "Run echo routed in the terminal and tell me its output." --wait --timeout 300`, then `control-openhands conversation events <id> --kinds ActionEvent,ObservationEvent,MessageEvent` (`<id>` from the start output). The first action is `route_task_to_model`, its observation starts `Classified task as 'model: deepseek-flash' and switched to LLM profile 'deepseek-flash'`, then the terminal runs `echo routed`. On the conversation page `control-openhands browser wait-text 'Switched to profile'` succeeds and `control-openhands browser screenshot --feature F12.route-first-message --name conversation` shows the `Switched to profile deepseek-flash` line above the answer. `control-openhands api GET "/api/conversations/<id>/events/search?limit=1" --max-bytes 200000` (the system prompt) contains `ROUTE_AT_CONVERSATION_START` and `"route_task_to_model"`. Switch **Run on first message** off (`control-openhands browser goto /settings/meta-llm` first: the browser is on the conversation), start `--prompt "Reply with only the word pong."`, and the same GET contains `"route_task_to_model"` but no `ROUTE_AT_CONVERSATION_START`; there is no route action.
scenarios.raw: **Routing in a conversation (`F12.route-first-message`).** Make `QA_router` active (row menu → Set active, `wait-text 'Meta-profile "QA_router" activated'`) with the switch on. Run `control-openhands conversation start --prompt "Run echo routed in the terminal and tell me its output." --wait --timeout 300`, then `control-openhands conversation events <id> --kinds ActionEvent,ObservationEvent,MessageEvent` (`<id>` from the start output). The first action is `route_task_to_model`, its observation starts `Classified task as 'model: deepseek-flash' and switched to LLM profile 'deepseek-flash'`, then the terminal runs `echo routed`. On the conversation page `control-openhands browser wait-text 'Switched to profile'` succeeds and `control-openhands browser screenshot --feature F12.route-first-message --name conversation` shows the `Switched to profile deepseek-flash` line above the answer. `control-openhands api GET "/api/conversations/<id>/events/search?limit=1" --max-bytes 200000` (the system prompt) contains `ROUTE_AT_CONVERSATION_START` and `"route_task_to_model"`. Switch **Run on first message** off (`control-openhands browser goto /settings/meta-llm` first: the browser is on the conversation), start `--prompt "Reply with only the word pong."`, and the same GET contains `"route_task_to_model"` but no `ROUTE_AT_CONVERSATION_START`; there is no route action.
expected: with a router active and the switch on, a new conversation routes its first message (`route_task_to_model` action, `Switched to profile <name>` in the chat); with the switch off the tool is still attached but the instruction is absent.

scenarios.name: F12--delete-the-active-router

scenarios.name: F12--router-activation-is-honest-on-acp
scenarios.title: Router activation is honest on ACP
scenarios.body:
ACP cannot attach the router; activation must report that refusal rather than plain success. Known failure (reproduced twice 2026-10-16, [OpenHands/software-agent-sdk#5879](https://github.com/OpenHands/software-agent-sdk/issues/5879)): actual global ACP settings produced an activated toast while both stored pointers stayed null. An active ACP profile pointer alone does not create this condition. The block restores the original owned settings bytes; its assertion rejects the misleading success toast.

  ```sh known-bug F12.activate acp-settings
  QA_ACP_SETTINGS="$OH_VERIFY_RUN/private/qa-known-acp-settings.json"
  cp "$OH_VERIFY_RUN/private/settings.json" "$QA_ACP_SETTINGS"
  trap 'cp "$QA_ACP_SETTINGS" "$OH_VERIFY_RUN/private/settings.json"; rm -f "$QA_ACP_SETTINGS"; control-openhands api DELETE /api/meta-profiles/QA_KNOWN_ACP_ROUTER --write >/dev/null; control-openhands browser reload >/dev/null' EXIT
  control-openhands api POST /api/meta-profiles/QA_KNOWN_ACP_ROUTER --data '{"classifier_model":"QA_KNOWN_CLASSIFIER","prompt_template":"Pick {{ instance_text }}"}' --write
  control-openhands api PATCH /api/settings --data '{"agent_settings_diff":{"agent_kind":"acp"}}' --write --pick agent_settings.agent_kind
  control-openhands assert --field value --equals acp -- api GET /api/settings --pick agent_settings.agent_kind
  control-openhands browser viewport desktop
  control-openhands browser goto /settings/meta-llm
  control-openhands browser wait 'testid=meta-profile-row-QA_KNOWN_ACP_ROUTER'
  control-openhands browser click 'testid=meta-profile-menu-trigger-QA_KNOWN_ACP_ROUTER'
  control-openhands browser click 'testid=meta-profile-set-active' --observe 'role=status' --observe-ms 1000
  control-openhands assert --field value --equals false --bug-shows true -- browser eval 'document.body.innerText.includes("Meta-profile \"QA_KNOWN_ACP_ROUTER\" activated")'  # bug
  ```

families.title: Agent profiles
families.overview:
Settings → Agent is a library of named agent profiles. Each profile is either an
OpenHands agent (an LLM profile, a system prompt, a tool set, parallel
tool calls, and MCP-server and secret scopes) or an ACP external agent (a preset
such as Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Pi or OpenCode, its launch command, a
model the agent itself reports, and provider credentials). One profile is
active; new conversations started from Home launch from it.
families.entry:
- Sidebar settings gear (`backend-selector-settings-link`): on desktop `/settings` redirects to `/settings/agents`. In the settings navigation, **Agent** (`sidebar-settings-/settings/agents`).
- Direct URL `/settings/agents`; the retired `/settings/agent` redirects there.
- Command menu (`Control+k`/`Meta+k` or `command-menu-trigger`): **Agent settings**.
- Getting-started checklist **Customize your agent** and the composer **+** → **Switch agent profile** → **Manage agent profiles** (both mapped in F09/F05).
- On Home, the composer **+** → **Switch agent profile** list activates a profile like **Set as active** (F05.agent-profile-switch).
- All per-profile actions are in the row's `...` menu (`agent-profile-menu-trigger`). The editor has no route: it replaces the list in place.
families.given:
Preconditions:

- Baseline state (launched, doctored, `onboard --skip` done) on a **fresh** run. `F13.editor-no-llm` must run before `control-openhands llm preset deepseek`; everything from `F13.stale-llm-ref` on needs the preset (`deepseek-flash` active, `deepseek-pro`).
- A fresh run has one profile, `default`, active, whose LLM profile is `default` (which does not exist). `control-openhands api GET /api/agent-profiles` shows it.
- `F13.mcp-scope` needs two configured MCP servers. Arrange them with `control-openhands api POST /api/settings/mcp/qa_mcp_a --data '{"transport":"stdio","command":"qa-no-such-command","enabled":false}' --write` and the same for `qa_mcp_b`.
- `F13.acp-conversation` needs the provider's agent CLI and an approved account; `F13.cloud-read-only` needs a Cloud organization member login. Both are blocked here.
- Dropdowns are autocompletes. Pick an option with `control-openhands browser choose 'testid=<testid>' '<label>'` (proven on `agent-type-selector`, `agent-preset-selector`, `agent-model-selector` (`Custom`), `agent-profile-llm-selector`, `agent-settings-mcp-mode` and `agent-settings-secrets-mode`). The manual opener, `control-openhands browser click 'div:has(> div > input[data-testid=<testid>]) >> role=button[name="Show suggestions"]'` then `browser click 'role=option[name="<label>"]'`, works for most of them but is flaky right after an editor opens (see Gotchas); clicking the input itself can open an empty, filtered list.
families.gotchas:
- The editor is not a route: `browser url` stays `/settings/agents` and `browser reload` drops unsaved edits back to the list. The settings page header (`settings-page-subtitle`) is hidden while it is open.
- Autocomplete dropdowns: clicking an input that already shows a value can open an empty listbox (the text filters it), and an option click then times out. The toggle-button opener does not always open the list either: on the Edit editor's `agent-profile-llm-selector` (bottom of the form) the option click timed out 5 of 5 times right after opening the editor, and the model list's `Custom` option once detached mid-click after a preset change. `browser choose` avoids the input-filtering problem, but an option may still remain unstable immediately after opening an editor. Reload and reopen before retrying; the suffix-identity check can use the already-selected active LLM without changing that dropdown. A listbox also closes if you spend a command (snapshot, eval) in between, so click the option right after opening.
- A taken name marks the field invalid with an alert reading `An agent profile with this name already exists. …`.
- `has-text=default` also matches the active row's `Default` badge (Playwright's text match ignores case), so with several profiles `'testid=agent-profile-row >> has-text=default'` hits two rows; select the seeded profile with `'testid=agent-profile-row >> nth=-1'` (it sorts last) or by its badge.
- Model lookups (`F13.acp-model-discovery`) spawn the provider CLI on the agent-server machine through npx with the profile's allowed secrets; they send no prompt. A failed lookup is retried each time the preset is picked again; a successful one is cached for about five minutes per preset and secret set.
- Switch rows are `sr-only` checkboxes inside labels (keyboard reachable): click the label text (`'testid=agent-settings-tool-list >> text=<tool>'`, `'testid=agent-settings-mcp-list >> text=<name>'`) and read `.checked` with `browser eval`. A bare `label` selector segment is parsed as `label=`, not CSS.
- The Default badge, the **Set as active** item and the `Switched to profile` toast all refer to the same active pointer; the wording differs from the LLM page (**Set as default**).
- The OpenHands row's grey text is the LLM profile name, not the kind. A fresh run's `default` shows `default` there although no LLM profile of that name exists until it is edited (`F13.stale-llm-ref`).
- Local seeded OpenHands `default` launches through global agent settings so the Skills selection applies; its per-profile fields do not apply on that path. Named profiles use their saved settings. Home launches follow the LLM pill. On a backend advertising per-launch LLM override, a named profile pinned to another LLM keeps its tool, concurrency and MCP settings; read `launched_agent_profile` and `agent` on the conversation (`F13.llm-pill-precedence`). Only older backends without that capability use the legacy settings fallback when the profile and pill differ.
- The ACP auth probe runs the provider CLI on the agent-server machine. If that machine has a Claude CLI login, Claude Code can show "already signed in". Use only an explicitly approved account for authenticated ACP checks.
- ACP credentials are global secrets, not profile fields: cancelling the editor saves nothing, but saving any ACP profile with a typed credential writes it to Settings → Secrets (F14) for every conversation.
- **Choose secrets** on an ACP profile also selects provider secret names that are not saved (`CODEX_AUTH_JSON`, `OPENAI_BASE_URL`); they show as switches without descriptions.
- The empty state (`agent-profiles-empty`) and the load-error state (`agent-profiles-load-error`) are not reachable on a local backend: deleting the last profile re-seeds `default`, and with the agent-server stopped the app swaps to **Manage backends** after a reload, or keeps the cached list without one.
- The refused-launch toast text comes from the Agent Server and changes between versions (`MCP server(s) not configured: <name>` on 1.53.0): assert that one toast names the server and the prompt stays, not the exact wording.
- Opening a row menu focuses its first enabled item. Arrows skip disabled **Set as active**; Escape closes the menu and returns focus to its trigger, while Tab closes it and continues normal tab order.
- The Add agent editor has its own agent description. Parallel tool calls label and description are translated.
- Known issue [#16905](https://github.com/OpenHands/OpenHands/issues/16905): An enabled built-in OpenHands skill can be absent from a new Claude Code ACP session. The enabled/disabled instruction-delivery check needs an approved authenticated Claude Code account, its ACP subprocess and the configured Code Review automation; no provider session is authorized here. (`F13.acp-conversation`).
- Known issue [#16296](https://github.com/OpenHands/OpenHands/issues/16296): Claude Code credential fields remain visible below the already-connected banner, leading users to think keys are required. The connected-state check needs an approved existing Claude CLI login on the agent-server host; a dummy credential does not prove that signed-in state. (`F13.acp-credentials`).
- Known issue [#17051](https://github.com/OpenHands/OpenHands/issues/17051): Codex ACP can work in New Chat while Issue-to-PR automation fails with missing OpenAI API credentials. Reproduction needs an approved Codex subscription login plus a configured Issue-to-PR automation and its repository credentials; the report does not identify the saved automation/profile settings. (`F13.acp-conversation`).
- Known issue [OpenHands/software-agent-sdk#5167](https://github.com/OpenHands/software-agent-sdk/issues/5167): On a headless Docker host an already usable Codex ChatGPT login can still time out during ACP authenticate. Reproduction needs an approved ChatGPT login in the reported headless/read-only-auth-file deployment and its adapter; a desktop or bogus login cannot establish this conditional trigger. (`F13.acp-conversation`).
- Known issue [OpenHands/software-agent-sdk#5995](https://github.com/OpenHands/software-agent-sdk/issues/5995): Claude Code ACP first turns with `claude-opus-5-5` can fail because the pinned adapter bundles an older Claude Code. Blocked: needs an approved Claude login/API key entitled to Opus5.5 and a real first turn; current SDK1.55 still pins the reported adapter0.63.0. No authenticated turn was attempted. (`F13.acp-conversation`, `F13.acp-model-discovery`).
- Known issue [OpenHands/software-agent-sdk#5899](https://github.com/OpenHands/software-agent-sdk/issues/5899): The browser tool can be reported unusable when genuine Chromium exists only under `PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH`. Blocked on this host: it has standard user Chrome. The distinguishing fixture needs a host/container with no standard/default-cache/PATH browser, plus a genuine custom-cache Chromium; never remove the user browser to create it. (`F13.openhands-options`; operational browser path F27).

features.description: under **Available Profiles**, rows (sorted by name) show the profile name, then its LLM profile (OpenHands) or `ACP (external subprocess)`, a **Default** badge on the active profile and a `...` menu (Edit, Set as active, Delete).
**Add agent profile** opens the editor; Save toasts `Profile "<name>" created` and the row is listed after a reload.

an empty or malformed name marks the field invalid (red rule) and disables Save; a name another profile already has also marks the field invalid, shows a red taken-name message about agent profiles under it (the rule stays grey) and disables Save (Edit accepts the profile's own name).
with no LLM profiles, an OpenHands profile shows `Create an LLM profile first to define an OpenHands agent.` and Save toasts `Select an LLM profile for this agent.` without creating anything.

OpenHands profiles offer an LLM profile dropdown (the active LLM profile by default), a **System prompt** choice (`OpenHands default`, `Default + your instructions` or `Custom persona`, each saved on the profile), **Parallel tool calls** (default 1, minimum 1) and **Tools**: `Standard tools` (default) lists the server's standard set read-only, `Choose tools` turns the server's tool catalog into switches; values persist and reopen.
Edit reopens the stored values with Save disabled until something changes; renaming keeps the profile id; Back and Cancel leave without saving.
editing a profile whose LLM profile no longer exists preselects the active LLM profile and enables Save, so saving heals the reference.
**Set as active** toasts `Switched to profile "<name>"`, moves the Default badge and is disabled on the active row.
a conversation started from Home after activation launches from that profile (its id and settings are stamped on the conversation).

when the active profile pins a different LLM profile than the Home LLM pill, a backend advertising per-launch LLM override uses the pill's LLM while preserving the named profile's other settings and identity.

**MCP servers** offers **All servers** (every configured server listed, switched on and disabled) or **Choose servers** (a switch per configured server); the choice persists; a chosen server that was removed stays listed with a red warning, and launching with it is refused.
**Secrets** offers **No profile restriction** (every switch on and disabled) or **Choose secrets**; on an ACP profile, Choose preselects that provider's secret names; the selection persists.

choosing **ACP (external subprocess)** shows Preset, Command, Credentials and Model; each preset prefills its command and its model choice (`Agent default`, or Gemini CLI's preferred `gemini-2.5-pro`), **Custom** empties the command and disables Save until one is typed, typing a preset's exact command selects that preset, and the Model list's **Custom** opens a free-text model field.

on a local backend the Preset list also offers **Pi** and **OpenCode** (with their own commands and credentials); a profile saved on them stores `acp_server` `pi`/`opencode` with `acp_command` `null`. On Cloud both are hidden (blocked here).

for a built-in preset with its default command the Model list comes from the agent: `Asking <agent> which models it offers…` while the agent-server asks it, then its models with `Agent default (<model>)` first; an agent that wants a login says `Sign in or add credentials above to see the models <agent> offers.`, one that cannot start says `<agent>'s models appear here after your first conversation with it. …`; a picked model is saved as `acp_model` and reopens selected.

built-in presets show a Credentials section (password fields), an auth banner (signed in / configured), a conflict warning for mutually exclusive Claude credentials, and `Already saved — leave blank to keep` for stored values. Credentials are saved as global secrets.

the Credentials fields follow the preset: Claude Code `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`, `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`; Codex `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `CODEX_AUTH_JSON` (multi-line), `OPENAI_BASE_URL`; Gemini CLI `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS_JSON` (multi-line), `GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT`, `GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION`, `GOOGLE_GENAI_USE_VERTEXAI`, `GEMINI_API_KEY`, `GEMINI_BASE_URL`; Pi `PI_AUTH_JSON` (multi-line), `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`; OpenCode `OPENCODE_AUTH_CONTENT` (multi-line), `OPENCODE_API_KEY`; **Custom** has no Credentials section. With no host login and no stored credential (Gemini here) no auth banner shows.

opening the row's `...` menu focuses Edit; ArrowDown/ArrowUp move focus between the enabled items (wrapping, and skipping the disabled **Set as active** on the active row), Enter runs the focused item, and Tab, Escape or a click outside close the menu.

Delete asks for confirmation; Cancel keeps the row, Delete removes it. Deleting the active profile selects `default` immediately; deleting the last profile makes the server re-seed and activate `default`.
the list, row menu and editor fit a 390 px viewport without horizontal overflow.
a conversation launched from an active ACP profile runs the external agent. Blocked without an approved provider account.
on a Cloud backend, organization members see rows without the `...` menu or **Add agent profile**. Blocked without a Cloud account.

scenarios.name: F13--name-rules
scenarios.title: Name rules
scenarios.body: In the Add editor, fill `testid=agent-profile-name-input` with `''`, `default`, `'bad name!'` and `QA_ok` in turn; after each run `control-openhands browser attr 'testid=agent-profile-name-input' aria-invalid` and `control-openhands browser enabled 'testid=save-agent-profile-btn'`. Results: `''` → `true`/`false`; `default` (duplicate) → `true`/`false`; `'bad name!'` → `true`/`false`; `QA_ok` → `false`/`true`. The rule under the field is always shown (grey) and turns the theme danger colour (`text-danger`, #18199) while the name is invalid; it reads `Profile name must start with a letter or digit, and contain only letters, digits, dots, underscores, or hyphens (max 64 characters)`. For the duplicate, `control-openhands browser count 'role=alert >> text=already exists'` is `1`: the alert is the field's description, in the danger colour (`rgb(231, 106, 94)` on OpenHands-Neutral, `rgb(209, 52, 56)` on Light+), while the rule text stays grey. It reads `An agent profile with this name already exists. Choose a different name, or edit the existing one.` Take `control-openhands browser screenshot --feature F13.name-validation --name duplicate` with `default` filled. In Edit the same message appears for another profile's name and not for the profile's own name (`F13.edit`).
scenarios.raw: **Name rules (`F13.name-validation`).** In the Add editor, fill `testid=agent-profile-name-input` with `''`, `default`, `'bad name!'` and `QA_ok` in turn; after each run `control-openhands browser attr 'testid=agent-profile-name-input' aria-invalid` and `control-openhands browser enabled 'testid=save-agent-profile-btn'`. Results: `''` → `true`/`false`; `default` (duplicate) → `true`/`false`; `'bad name!'` → `true`/`false`; `QA_ok` → `false`/`true`. The rule under the field is always shown (grey) and turns the theme danger colour (`text-danger`, #18199) while the name is invalid; it reads `Profile name must start with a letter or digit, and contain only letters, digits, dots, underscores, or hyphens (max 64 characters)`. For the duplicate, `control-openhands browser count 'role=alert >> text=already exists'` is `1`: the alert is the field's description, in the danger colour (`rgb(231, 106, 94)` on OpenHands-Neutral, `rgb(209, 52, 56)` on Light+), while the rule text stays grey. It reads `An agent profile with this name already exists. Choose a different name, or edit the existing one.` Take `control-openhands browser screenshot --feature F13.name-validation --name duplicate` with `default` filled. scenarios.name: F13--acp-form

scenarios.body: In the Add editor run `control-openhands browser click 'testid=agent-type-selector'` and `control-openhands browser click 'role=option[name="ACP (external subprocess)"]'`. `control-openhands browser value 'testid=agent-preset-selector'` is `Claude Code`, `browser value 'testid=agent-command-input'` is `npx -y --prefer-offline @agentclientprotocol/claude-agent-acp@0.63.0` and `browser value 'testid=agent-model-selector'` is `Agent default`; `agent-profile-no-llm` is gone (ACP needs no LLM profile). The preset list (`control-openhands browser click 'div:has(> div > input[data-testid=agent-preset-selector]) >> role=button[name="Show suggestions"]'`, then `control-openhands browser snapshot 'role=listbox'`) is `Claude Code`, `Codex`, `Gemini CLI`, `Pi`, `OpenCode`, `Custom` (`browser press Escape`). Pick `Codex` and `Gemini CLI` from `testid=agent-preset-selector`: the command becomes `npx -y --prefer-offline @agentclientprotocol/codex-acp@1.10.0` / `npx -y --prefer-offline @google/gemini-cli@0.46.0 --acp` and the model `Agent default` / `gemini-2.5-pro` (the models come from the agent since #18131: `F13.acp-model-discovery`). Pick `Custom`: the command is empty and Save is disabled. `control-openhands browser fill 'testid=agent-command-input' 'npx -y qa-custom-acp --stdio'` enables Save. Model override: with a built-in preset, run `control-openhands browser choose 'testid=agent-model-selector' 'Custom'` (or open the model list with its toggle button and `control-openhands browser click 'role=option[name="Custom"][exact]'`); `control-openhands browser count 'testid=agent-model-input'` is `1` and empty. The **Custom** preset shows `agent-model-input` directly (no model list).

Pick `Custom`: the command is empty and Save is disabled. `control-openhands browser fill 'testid=agent-command-input' 'npx -y qa-custom-acp --stdio'` enables Save. Filling the exact Codex command flips the preset to `Codex`; appending ` --verbose` flips it back to `Custom`. scenarios.name: F13--create-an-acp-profile

scenarios.name: F13--models-from-the-agent
scenarios.title: Models from the agent
scenarios.body: In a new ACP editor, each built-in preset pick first shows (unless a successful lookup for that preset and secret set is cached, about 5 minutes: OpenCode then skips it) `control-openhands browser text 'testid=agent-model-discovering'` `Asking <agent> which models it offers…` (the agent-server runs the agent CLI through npx for `POST /api/acp/models`; the first lookup can take a minute while npx downloads it). Wait with `control-openhands browser wait 'testid=agent-model-discovering' --state detached --timeout 120000`, then read `control-openhands browser testids --hidden --filter agent-model`. In this sandbox (no Claude, Codex, Gemini or Pi login for the agent-server): Claude Code fails to start and shows `agent-model-list-after-first-conversation` (`Claude Code's models appear here after your first conversation with it. You can also switch models from the chat.`); Codex, Gemini CLI and Pi need a login and show `agent-model-discovery-needs-auth` (`Sign in or add credentials above to see the models <agent> offers.`), with the model left at `Agent default` (`gemini-2.5-pro` for Gemini); `<run>/private/stack.log` logs `ACP model discovery failed: server=<key> code=ACPInitError|ACPAuthRequired`. OpenCode needs no key: `browser value 'testid=agent-model-selector'` is `Agent default (OpenCode/Big Pickle)` and the list (open it with `browser click 'div:has(> div > input[data-testid=agent-model-selector]) >> role=button[name="Show suggestions"]'`, then `browser snapshot 'role=listbox'`) has that entry, a non-empty list of the models OpenCode reports live (12 on 2026-10-13, such as `OpenCode/Big Pickle` and `OpenCode/Exo Free`) and `Custom` (screenshot `--feature F13.acp-model-discovery --name opencode-models`). Edit `QA_opencode`: Save is disabled until `control-openhands browser choose 'testid=agent-model-selector' 'OpenCode/Exo Free'`; Save (`Profile "QA_opencode" updated`) stores `acp_model` `opencode/exo-free`, and reopening shows `OpenCode/Exo Free` with Save disabled. With a saved `OPENAI_API_KEY` (even a dummy, `F13.acp-credentials`) Codex lists its models and shows `Agent default (GPT-6-Astra)`. Lookups never add a conversation to the list (`api GET "/api/conversations/search?limit=20"` stays empty).

You can also switch models from the chat.`); Codex, Gemini CLI and Pi need a login and show `agent-model-discovery-needs-auth` (`Sign in or add credentials above to see the models <agent> offers.`), with the model left at `Agent default` (`gemini-2.5-pro` for Gemini); `<run>/private/stack.log` logs `ACP model discovery failed: server=<key> code=ACPInitError|ACPAuthRequired`. scenarios.name: F13--edit-and-rename

scenarios.name: F13--credentials
scenarios.title: Credentials
scenarios.body: In a new ACP editor with preset `Claude Code`, `control-openhands browser testids --hidden --filter acp` lists `settings-acp-secret-CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`, `-ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `-ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` and one banner (`settings-acp-auth-detected` when the agent-server machine has a Claude CLI login: `You're already signed in to Claude Code — you can leave the fields below blank.`). `control-openhands browser attr 'testid=settings-acp-secret-ANTHROPIC_API_KEY' type` is `password`. Fill `settings-acp-secret-CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` with `qa-dummy-oauth` and `settings-acp-secret-ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` with `qa-dummy-key`; `control-openhands browser text 'testid=acp-credential-conflict-warning'` is `Setting ANTHROPIC_API_KEY alongside CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN breaks its authentication — leave one of them blank.` (screenshot `--feature F13.acp-credentials --name conflict` after `browser scroll 'testid=acp-credential-conflict-warning'`). scenarios.name: F13--openhands-options
scenarios.title: OpenHands options
scenarios.body:
Click `testid=add-agent-profile`, fill the name `QA_oh`. Defaults: `browser value` on `testid=agent-profile-llm-selector` is the active LLM profile (`deepseek-flash (deepseek/deepseek-flash)`), on `testid=agent-settings-system-prompt-mode` `OpenHands default`, on `testid=agent-settings-tools-mode` `Standard tools` and on `testid=sdk-settings-tool_concurrency_limit` `1`; `control-openhands browser text 'testid=agent-settings-tool-list'` lists `file_editor`, `task_tracker`, `terminal` and `switch_llm` with their descriptions (the list follows the Agent Server; it also includes `browser_tool_set` when usable). Run `control-openhands browser choose 'testid=agent-settings-tools-mode' 'Choose tools'`; `control-openhands browser eval "[...document.querySelectorAll('[data-testid=agent-settings-tool-list] input')].map(i=>i.dataset.testid.replace('agent-settings-tool-','')+'='+i.checked)"` is the selected standard tools, including `file_editor=true`, `task_tracker=true`, `terminal=true` and `switch_llm=true`; `task_tool_set=false`, `glob=false` and `grep=false`. Additional rows follow the current server catalog. Click `'testid=agent-settings-tool-list >> text=switch_llm'` and `'testid=agent-settings-tool-list >> text=task_tool_set'` (the eval flips both). Fill `testid=sdk-settings-tool_concurrency_limit` with `0` and click Save: `browser toasts` shows `Parallel tool calls must be at least 1` and `browser eval "document.querySelector('[data-testid=sdk-settings-tool_concurrency_limit]').validationMessage"` is `Value must be greater than or equal to 1.` Fill `2`, `control-openhands browser choose 'testid=agent-profile-llm-selector' 'deepseek-pro (deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro)'`, Save (`Profile "QA_oh" created`), `browser reload`: the row reads `QA_oh` / `deepseek-pro`, and `api GET /api/agent-profiles/QA_oh` has `llm_profile_ref` `deepseek-pro`, `tools` retaining the selected standard tools plus `task_tool_set` (including `task_tracker`), `enable_classify_and_switch_llm_tool` `false` and `tool_concurrency_limit` `2`. Reopening shows `Choose tools` with the same switches, `2` and `deepseek-pro`, with Save disabled. (There are no **Enable sub-agents** or **Let the agent switch LLM profiles** switches: `browser count 'text=Enable sub-agents'` is `0`.)
  System prompt: reopen `QA_oh`, `control-openhands browser choose 'testid=agent-settings-system-prompt-mode' 'Default + your instructions'` and fill `testid=agent-settings-system-prompt` with `Use terse QA answers.`. Save, `browser reload` and reopen: `api GET /api/agent-profiles/QA_oh` has `system_message_suffix` `Use terse QA answers.` and `persona` `null`, and the editor keeps the mode and text with Save disabled. Then choose `Custom persona`, fill `You are the disposable QA persona.`, Save, reload and reopen: `persona` is that text, `system_message_suffix` is `null`, and the editor keeps the mode and text. Choose `OpenHands default` and Save (both fields `null`) before later checks that use this profile.

scenarios.name: F13--pill-wins-over-a-pinned-llm
scenarios.title: Pill wins over a pinned LLM
scenarios.body: With `QA_oh` active (pinned to `deepseek-pro`) and the Home pill on `deepseek-flash` (`browser text 'testid=chat-input-llm-profile'` on `/`), run `control-openhands conversation start --prompt "Reply with only: qa-profile-ok. Do not run tools." --wait --timeout 240`. The output's `model` is `deepseek/deepseek-flash`. On the current backend, `control-openhands api GET /api/conversations/<id>` (id from that output) has `launched_agent_profile.agent_profile_id` equal to QA_oh's id, `launched_agent_profile.llm_profile_ref` `deepseek-flash`, and `agent.tool_concurrency_limit` `2`: the per-launch LLM override keeps the named profile's other settings. These metadata checks can be made before a successful reply; a refused-loopback fixture proves the launch configuration only.

Do not run tools." --wait --timeout 240`. The output's `model` is `deepseek/deepseek-flash`. On the current backend, `control-openhands api GET /api/conversations/<id>` (id from that output) has `launched_agent_profile.agent_profile_id` equal to QA_oh's id, `launched_agent_profile.llm_profile_ref` `deepseek-flash`, and `agent.tool_concurrency_limit` `2`: the per-launch LLM override keeps the named profile's other settings. expected: when the active profile pins a different LLM profile than the Home LLM pill, a backend advertising per-launch LLM override uses the pill's LLM while preserving the named profile's other settings and identity.
