families.title: Backends, Cloud and sharing
families.overview:
One Canvas can drive several agent servers. The backend selector at the bottom
of the sidebar lists every registered backend with a live status dot and
switches between them; its footer opens **Add Backend** (OpenHands Cloud login
through an OAuth device flow, or a local/remote agent server by host and API
key) and **Manage Backends** (select, edit, remove, and Cloud "Log back in").
When the active backend is unreachable the whole app is replaced by Manage
backends in recovery mode. Cloud backends add organization rows, a Cloud
settings link and public sharing of conversations (read-only at
`/shared/conversations/:id`); `/oauth/device/verify` is the device-approval page.
When the page is served with the DigitalOcean Managed Agents bridge (the
desktop app's preload, or the web server's own bridge, which the launcher's
ingress mounts by default behind the session key), Add Backend gains a
**Providers** tab whose DigitalOcean entry signs in with a personal access
token and turns a Managed Agents session into a backend.
Everything except the Cloud and DigitalOcean accounts themselves can be driven
locally with a second `control-openhands` stack as the extra backend.
families.entry:
- Sidebar, bottom: the backend selector (`backend-selector`; click or hover) → options, **Add Backend** (`add-backend-menu-item`), **Manage Backends** (`manage-backends-menu-item`).
- Collapsed rail: hover the backend icon (`collapsed-backend-selector-link`) → the same footer items.
- Phone: hamburger (`sidebar-mobile-menu-toggle`) → drawer → backend selector.
- Manage backends → **Add Backend** (`manage-backends-add`) opens the same Add form.
- Direct URLs: any in-app URL with `?backend=<id>`; `/oauth/device/verify[?user_code=CODE]`; `/shared/conversations/<id>`.
- Conversation header name → "..." (`conversation-name >> ellipsis-button`) for Public Share (Cloud only).
- Reloading with an unreachable active backend opens the recovery gate.
- Onboarding's backend step and the public-mode API-key screen also add backends; they belong to F01. The ChatGPT subscription card is F10 (`F10.subscription`) and the provider balance card is F27 (`F27.usage-provider-balance`).
families.given:
Preconditions:

- Baseline state (launched, doctored, `onboard --skip` done) and `control-openhands llm preset deepseek` on this run.
- One conversation on this run: `control-openhands conversation start --prompt "Reply with exactly: QA_F25_PONG" --wait --timeout 180`; note its `<id>`. The conversation only has to exist: F25 never reads the reply, so a run that ends in `error` (for example a key without balance, saved with `llm preset deepseek --no-validate`) is enough.
- A second stack to add as a backend, started without a browser and never driven directly: `export OH_VERIFY_RUN_2=$(OH_VERIFY_RUN= control-openhands launch --new --build never --no-browser --print-run)`, then `control-openhands status --run "$OH_VERIFY_RUN_2"`; its `baseUrl` is `<second-url>` below and its key is `$OH_VERIFY_RUN_2/private/session-key`. It has no conversations.
- No backend named `QA_Second` or `QA_Renamed` exists (the selector lists only `Local`).
- Bullets run in order: Add creates `QA_Second`, Edit renames it to `QA_Renamed`, Remove deletes it.
- The Managed Agents rows need the bridge, which every `control-openhands launch` run has: `control-openhands browser eval "!!window.marsBridge"` is `true` and `curl -s <baseUrl>/mars/health` answers `{"ok":true,"authRequired":true}`. `F25.digitalocean-agents` and `F25.digitalocean-backend-removal` stay blocked without a DigitalOcean account.
- Cloud account: where this machine's proxy injects OpenHands Cloud credentials (`curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' https://app.all-hands.dev/api/organizations` is `200` without a token), the **Cloud backend** bullet below can approve the device flow in its popup; otherwise it is blocked. Blocked here even with such an account: `F25.cloud-log-back-in` (needs a logged-out Cloud row), org switching in `F25.cloud-org-rows` (needs a second organization), the archived and error states of `F25.cloud-sandbox-states`, `F25.cloud-org-suspended` (also needs a suspended OpenHands Enterprise organization or membership), `F25.share-publicly` (toggle), and `F25.locked-cloud`, which also needs a launcher flag (see Gotchas).
families.gotchas:
- Export the second run as `OH_VERIFY_RUN_2` and pass it with `--run`; never export it as `OH_VERIFY_RUN`, or the browser commands look for a browser that run does not have. `OH_VERIFY_RUN= control-openhands launch --new ...` keeps the launch from reusing this run.
- The second backend asks its own telemetry consent the first time it becomes active, over whatever page you are on; `onboard --skip` answers it. Consent is stored per backend, so a later `restart` of the second run does not ask again.
- `browser fill <sel> --value-file FILE` takes no positional value; it keeps the key out of the shell history and the evidence. Edit forms show the stored key masked, but `browser snapshot` of the Edit form prints it in clear: do not save that snapshot as evidence with a real key.
- Manage-row test ids use the backend name (`manage-backends-row-QA_Second`), so they change after a rename and are not unique when two backends share a name; the Cloud **Log back in** id uses the backend id instead (`manage-backends-login-<id>-login-button`).
- Selector options are named `<status> <name>` (`Connected Local`, `Disconnected QA_Renamed`): select them with `role=option[name="Connected <name>"]`.
- After a navigating option click, `--expect-url` must allow `?backend=...`: end regexes with `(\?|$)`.
- `browser wait-tab <regex>` matches any open page, including the current one, unless `--new` leaves out the tab the daemon is on: for a second tab at the same URL (`/conversations` from **New Chat**) use `wait-tab '/conversations$' --new`, or read `browser tabs` and switch with `browser tab <i>`. `browser tab new /conversations` opens a plain second tab (no opener, empty sessionStorage), the state a user reaches by opening the app again. Close extra tabs highest index first, or the indexes shift under you.
- `browser tab new` switches the daemon to the tab it opened, so a `wait-tab <regex> --new` run right after it reports the tab you came from (`index` `0` with two tabs); `browser tab 0` first when you want the new tab's index from `wait-tab`. A `tab new` and a `click --modifiers Control` on **New Chat** reach the same state (selector from the localStorage fallback, sessionStorage item `null`).
- A tab opened with `click --modifiers Control` starts with an empty sessionStorage, so it boots from the localStorage fallback (the backend last chosen in any tab) unless its URL carries `?backend=`. Opening a `?backend=` link writes that backend to localStorage too: a per-tab check that relies on "last choice" must run before opening pinned links.
- The Add Backend Agent-server form has no inline "required" messages; it only disables **Connect**. The messages exist in the Edit form.
- Footer clicks from the collapsed popover or the phone drawer open the modals a moment later: `browser wait` for them instead of `count`.
- The device-flow popup survives errors: every failed attempt leaves an `about:blank` tab ([#17953](https://github.com/OpenHands/OpenHands/issues/17953)). Cancel closes it; after an error close it with `browser close-tab`.
- With the default host the device flow talks to the real `app.all-hands.dev` (`POST /oauth/device/authorize`, then token polling). Starting and cancelling is harmless; approve a code only in the **Cloud backend** bullet, with an account you may use.
- While the second stack's agent server is stopped or restarting, its ingress answers without CORS headers, so the browser logs `Access to fetch at '<second-url>/api/settings' ... blocked by CORS policy` (also `/server_info`, `/api/conversations/search`, `/api/llm/models/verified`). That is the dead upstream, not a CORS bug; a healthy second stack sends `access-control-allow-origin` for this origin.
- Expected: Escape never clears the backend selector. Known failure (reproduced 2026-10-09, 2026-10-12, 2026-10-13 and 2026-10-14, [#18233](https://github.com/OpenHands/OpenHands/issues/18233)): Escape on the focused backend selector while its menu is closed (a second Escape after the one that closes the menu, and sometimes the Escape that closes Manage Backends opened from it) clears the selection: the closed selector shows the active backend's name as an italic placeholder (`browser value 'testid=backend-selector >> role=combobox'` is `""`) and its status dot is gone, so `browser wait 'testid=backend-selector >> role=status[name="Disconnected"]'` times out although the backend is down; a reload restores it. Reload before a closed-selector status check, as the Edit bullet does. Repro: `browser click 'testid=backend-selector'`, `browser press Escape` twice ([#18233](https://github.com/OpenHands/OpenHands/issues/18233)). On 2026-10-12 `bug proof` verified fix PR #18238 at 77de0ad24 against main f07aebdf5 (two `xfail`, two `xpass`, desktop). `control-openhands bug run F25.selector-dropdown` replays it (desktop, after a reload with the mouse off the selector: a reload under a mouse left on it opens its menu and empties its field, which would look like the bug) and reports `xfail` while the bug lasts:

  ```sh known-bug F25.selector-dropdown escape-closed
  control-openhands browser viewport desktop
  control-openhands browser goto /
  control-openhands browser hover 'testid=root-layout'
  control-openhands browser reload
  control-openhands browser wait 'testid=backend-selector >> role=status[name="Connected"]' --timeout 15000
  control-openhands assert --field value --equals Local -- browser value 'testid=backend-selector >> role=combobox'
  control-openhands browser click 'testid=backend-selector'
  control-openhands browser press Escape
  control-openhands browser press Escape
  control-openhands browser screenshot 'testid=backend-selector' --feature F25.selector-dropdown --name escape-closed
  control-openhands assert --field value --equals Local --bug-shows '' -- browser value 'testid=backend-selector >> role=combobox'  # bug
  ```
- Local and remote backends are probed every 30 s (settings + server_info), Cloud backends every 5 min (#18128), so allow up to 40 s for a local dot to change. `browser network --clear`, wait about 70 s, then `browser network --filter server_info` shows two probes per local origin 30 s apart. While the active backend is down, any reload lands on the recovery gate: drive the disconnected rows on the page that was already loaded.
- `/oauth/device/verify` is a Cloud page that also ships in Canvas: on a local stack its POST target does not exist, so Authorize always ends in `Error`. The "Authentication Required" state is unreachable (`useIsAuthed` always resolves `true`).
- `/shared/conversations/<id>` on a local backend also raises a raw toast `HTTP request failed (404 Not Found): {"detail":"Not Found"}` next to `Conversation not found` ([#17953](https://github.com/OpenHands/OpenHands/issues/17953)).
- Known failure (repro candidate, not an exemption): `F25.edit-escape` closes the Manage modal underneath and drops the Edit draft (Cancel and X close only Edit, `F25.edit-cancel`) ([#17953](https://github.com/OpenHands/OpenHands/issues/17953)).
- The add bullet's `network --external --filter 'ids='` check guards an earlier race: [#18390](https://github.com/OpenHands/OpenHands/issues/18390) tracks the same first-activation symptom; on a backend's first activation from `/conversations/<id>`, about 1 attempt in 5 asked the new backend for the old conversation id. It did not happen in 15 first activations at 4eff80237: each time `QA_Second` was removed, its consent unset with `control-openhands api PATCH /api/settings --run "$OH_VERIFY_RUN_2" --write --data '{"misc_settings_diff":{"app_preferences":{"user_consents_to_analytics":null}}}'` (arrange only) and the backend added again from `/conversations/<id>`. A backend that lacks an id answers `[null]`, which now reads as "not found" (only the `This conversation does not exist…` toast), not as incompatible data. No merged change was shown to fix the race itself (#18009 only changed how a `[null]` answer reads; #18024 only moved the redirect into a shared hook, still called after `addBackend`), so a hit (an `ids=` request to `<second-url>`) is a bug to file. At 95115e84f6dd it hit on 1 of 2 first activations from `/conversations/<id>` (one `GET <second-url>/api/conversations?ids=<id>` answered `200`, with no `This conversation does not exist…` toast after it). The hit followed a failed Connect in the same modal (an empty key, `Invalid API key`) before the successful one; the clean retry, which connected once, had none, so a repro should try both sequences. On 2026-10-08 at d2c89252d it did not reproduce in 17 first activations (8 clean, 9 failed-then-clean, some under CPU load and some human-paced): every `ids=` capture was empty, and no merged change touched the activation logic since the hit, so it stays a watch item rather than a filed defect. Record the Add bullet as `fail` when the request appears, even though the redirect and the selector look right. Known failure (reproduced 2026-10-13, #18390): two independent first activations hit it that day, each the run's first activation of `QA_Second` after a clean Connect. On 2026-10-13 at 2bdc0e9d6 it hit on 1 of 6 first activations from `/conversations/<id>`: the first one of the run (`GET <second-url>/api/conversations?ids=<id>` `200`, no toast), a clean Connect in a modal opened after earlier failed Connects in other Add Backend openings; the next 5 (2 failed-then-clean, 3 clean, plus one Manage → Add) had none.
- Add Backend and Manage Backends take and keep keyboard focus, and Edit backend takes it on open (`ModalBackdrop`; at phone width open the selector with `'testid=sidebar-mobile-drawer >> testid=backend-selector'`, since the bare test id matches two selectors). At desktop width focus returns to the selector input when they close (at phone width Add Backend's X closes the drawer too and focus falls to the page body), so an Escape pressed after closing lands on the selector and can trigger [#18233](https://github.com/OpenHands/OpenHands/issues/18233) below.
- Toasts are not page or HTTP errors, so `browser errors --app-only` misses them: read `browser toasts --history` after every add or switch, before anything reloads the page (the history starts with each page load).
- `F25.locked-cloud` needs `scripts/static-server.mjs --lock-to-cloud <url>`, which neither `bin/agent-canvas.mjs` nor `control-openhands launch` can pass today; even with it, reconnecting needs a Cloud account.
- The Cloud tab title truncates to `OpenHan…` at 390 px when the Agent-server tab is selected; the layout still fits. With the Providers tab present all three titles are cut to three letters.
- A token DigitalOcean rejects surfaces as the bare `401 Unauthorized`, with no hint that the token is wrong or lacks scopes.
- Known issue [#18029](https://github.com/OpenHands/OpenHands/issues/18029) (`F25.locked-cloud`): A returning user in a locked Cloud deployment can reach the no-backend placeholder and fail to start conversations despite a healthy configured backend. The report proposes a stale document or alternate origin but does not capture which occurred. Recheck against the affected locked deployment with a Cloud session, its exact origin, cache response headers and injected host state; the normal local launcher does not reproduce this deployment condition.
- Known issue [#17390](https://github.com/OpenHands/OpenHands/issues/17390) (`F25.cloud-sandbox-states`): Every sent Cloud message can fail with `token_not_found_in_db` from the model proxy. Recheck with the affected Cloud account/session and a minimal no-tools prompt; capture the error type with provider token text and hashes redacted. The report supplies no deployment version or deterministic token-provisioning sequence, and this run has no Cloud account.
- Known issue [#17163](https://github.com/OpenHands/OpenHands/issues/17163) (`F25.cloud-sandbox-states`): A Free Cloud account can lose access to previously usable models with HTTP 403 and a team-restriction message despite no team being created. Recheck with the affected account and its model entitlement/org history; local credentials cannot prove Cloud eligibility and this run has no such account.
- Known issue [#16874](https://github.com/OpenHands/OpenHands/issues/16874) (`F25.cloud-sandbox-states`): A failed resume of a paused Cloud sandbox was reported to consume a one-shot guard and leave chat disconnected until remount. Current source uses a retrying resume hook, so recheck the original failure and a second pause in one route mount before concluding resolution. Blocked without a real paused Cloud sandbox and a controlled one-request backend/network failure; source changes alone are not a live pass.
- Known issue [#15676](https://github.com/OpenHands/OpenHands/issues/15676) (`F25.cloud-sandbox-states`): Refreshing an approximately 24-hour-old Cloud conversation on Vercel can fail to resume/reconnect. Recheck an authenticated affected Cloud deployment with an aged sandbox/session and exact console/network error; the report omits its commit and failure text, and no aged Cloud fixture is available here.
- Known issue [#15822](https://github.com/OpenHands/OpenHands/issues/15822) (`F25.switch-backend` `F25.health-status` `F25.cloud-org-rows`): Cloud-proxy traffic was reported to continue after switching from Cloud to Local. Current source probes registered inactive Cloud backends on a five-minute cadence; recheck the reported repeated OPTIONS behavior with a real registered Cloud account/org and capture only credential-redacted request metadata after switching. This run has no authenticated Cloud backend.
- Known issue [OpenHands/automation#565](https://github.com/OpenHands/automation/issues/565) (`F25.cloud-org-rows`, `F25.cloud-org-suspended`): An org-scoped Cloud automation request with an unauthorized `X-Org-Id` can turn the identity service's 403 into a misleading 502/outage page. Recheck with an authenticated Cloud org-bound key and a disposable unauthorized organization id, comparing automation list and the identity response while preserving credential redaction. Local mode bypasses this identity service and cannot reproduce it.
- Known issue [OpenHands/software-agent-sdk#5789](https://github.com/OpenHands/software-agent-sdk/issues/5789) (`F25.add-agent-server`, `F25.health-status`): a deferred-init Agent Server can report ready after accepting a GUI origin through `/api/init`, while browser preflights from that origin still fail and Canvas cannot connect. Recheck an owned warm-pool server initialized with the actual non-localhost Canvas origin and compare admission with an origin supplied at server boot. The default loopback-origin stack is already allowed and cannot exercise this branch.

features.description: clicking (or hovering) the selector opens a listbox of backends, each option named `<status> <name>` with a status dot, and a footer with **Add Backend** and **Manage Backends**.

**Add Backend** opens "Choose how you want to connect" with a description, a **Learn more** link to the deployment docs and the tabs **OpenHands Cloud** (selected) and **Agent-server** (plus **Providers** with the bridge, see the Providers row). It takes keyboard focus on open (the close button), Tab and Shift+Tab wrap inside it, and at desktop width closing returns focus to the backend selector (at phone width the drawer closes with the modal and focus falls back to the page body). Escape does not close it; the X does.
on the Cloud tab, **Advanced** reveals a **Host** field (placeholder `https://app.all-hands.dev`) for a self-hosted Cloud.

**Connect to OpenHands** opens a popup and shows `Starting authentication...`, then `Waiting for authorization...` with the verification link and **Cancel**; Cancel returns to the idle button and closes the popup. An unreachable host shows `Failed to start device flow: ...` with **Try again**. Approving the code (adds a backend named OpenHands Cloud) needs a Cloud account.

the Agent-server tab has a **Local / Remote** toggle. Local shows a collapsible **Before you connect** with `agent-canvas --backend-only --port 8001` and a local-setup docs link; Remote shows **Recommended setup**, **Connection details** and a remote-setup docs link.

**Connect** stays disabled until Host Name and a valid Host are filled; the API Key field is optional for Connect on Local and required on Remote, but a key-protected host still rejects an empty key. A dead host, an empty key or a wrong key shows `Could not connect to <host>` with the reason inline (`Disconnected (check URL or network)` for a dead host, `Invalid API key` for an empty or wrong key); a reachable host with the right key, entered on the default Local location, adds the backend, makes it active (BM-001) and redirects a `/conversations/<id>` page to `/conversations` without an error toast, also on the backend's first activation, without asking the new backend for the old conversation id.

choosing another option shows a full-screen `Switching to <name>` overlay for about a second, then the sidebar and pages show that backend's data; on `/conversations/<id>` the app moves to `/conversations` (BM-002).
in-app links carry `?backend=<id>`; opening such a URL pins the tab to that backend; an unknown id is ignored.

the active backend is per browser tab: switching it in one tab leaves the other open tabs where they were, a new tab opened from a plain link starts from the last choice made in any tab, and a sidebar conversation row opened in a new tab (Control-click) lands on the backend that owns the conversation because its link carries `?backend=<owner>`.

Manage backends lists every backend with status dot, name, version (`v1.50.1`), host, status text and a LOCAL/CLOUD pill, plus Edit and Remove; it takes keyboard focus on open and keeps Tab inside; Escape, a backdrop click, X and **Done** close it and return focus to the selector.
**Add Backend** in Manage backends opens the same Add form stacked over Manage; its X returns to Manage, and a successful add keeps Manage open with the new row while the new backend becomes active.
clicking a healthy row makes that backend active and closes the modal; on a detail page it leaves it for that section's list, like the selector does (BM-002).

the pencil opens "Edit backend" pre-filled (key masked) with a `Connected · Local v<version>` badge; empty name and invalid host show `Name is required` and `Enter a valid URL (e.g. http://localhost:8080)` and disable Save; Save re-tests the connection, keeps the modal open with `Could not connect to <host>` on failure, and persists on success.
**Cancel** and the X in Edit backend close only the Edit modal and discard the draft; Manage backends stays open with the stored values.
Escape in the Edit modal should not discard the draft (the modal disables Escape). Known failure, see Gotchas.

a backend that stops answering turns its dot red (`Disconnected`) within one health probe (every 30 s for local and remote agent servers; Cloud backends every 5 min and not on window focus or reconnect, #18128); its Manage row reads `Disconnected (check URL or network)` with a red detail line and cannot be selected.

reloading while the active backend is down shows only `agent-server-onboarding-screen` with Manage backends in recovery mode (no X, no Done, Escape ignored, primary **Add Backend**); choosing a healthy row restores the app.
the trash icon asks `Remove backend "<name>"? If it is active, the app will switch back to Local.`; Cancel keeps it, Confirm removes it and an active removed backend falls back to Local (BM-003).
with the rail collapsed, the backend icon's popover offers the same Add Backend and Manage Backends items, and both modals open.

at 390 px the drawer's selector opens Add and Manage inside the viewport without horizontal overflow. Edit backend fits at 320 and 390 px; on short viewports its form scrolls while the title and close control stay visible, and Cancel/Save remain reachable.

`/oauth/device/verify` shows a "Device Authorization" code form; with `?user_code=` it shows "Device Authorization Request", the code, a Security Notice and Cancel / Authorize Device. On a local stack Authorize and Continue end in the `Error` card with **Try Again**.
`/shared/conversations/<id>` is a standalone read-only page (no app shell); on a local backend it reads `Conversation not found`.
on a Cloud backend the conversation menu has a **Public Share** toggle with copy-link and open-link buttons; on a local backend the item is absent.
each Cloud backend appears once per organization as `<name> – <org>` (`Personal Workspace` for the user's own), and choosing one scopes lists to that org.
a logged-out Cloud row shows `Logged out` and a **Log back in** button that reruns the device flow.
with a Cloud backend active the gear next to the selector opens `<cloud host>/settings?org=<org>` in a new tab.
Cloud conversations show waiting, archived and error sandbox states in chat.

when a Cloud call made for the selected organization (`X-Org-Id`) fails with 403 and `detail` `Organization is suspended` or `User membership is suspended`, the app is replaced by `<org> is suspended. Contact your administrator to restore access.` (or `Your access to <org> is suspended. Contact your administrator to restore it.`), then `Switch to another workspace` and one button per other organization (`Personal Workspace` for the user's own). A button selects that organization and the app returns; with no other organization only the message shows. A reload clears the in-memory record. Blocked here: needs an OpenHands Enterprise instance with `ENABLE_SUPER_ADMIN` where a Super Admin suspended the organization or this member's membership, signed in as a non-Super-Admin member with that organization selected (#17988).

only when the page has the Managed Agents bridge (`window.marsBridge`), Add Backend shows a third tab **Providers** ("Connect through DigitalOcean and more.") with a **DigitalOcean** card ("Your team's OpenHands agents") and `More providers coming soon.`. Every launcher-served web page has it (the ingress answers `/mars/health`); without it (`MARS_WEB=0`, or a non-loopback bind with no session key at all) there are only the Cloud and Agent-server tabs and no Managed Agents UI anywhere. A non-loopback bind that has a key (F26 `--host 0.0.0.0` with `LOCAL_BACKEND_API_KEY`) mounts the bridge behind that key and offers the tab too, although the page itself carries no key (see the sign-in bullet's Known failure).

the DigitalOcean card opens "Connect your DigitalOcean team" with a Back button, a masked **Personal access token** field, a **Create a token** link to `https://cloud.digitalocean.com/account/api/tokens` and **Connect with token**, disabled until a token is typed (the **Sign in with DigitalOcean** OAuth button exists only in the desktop app). A token of the wrong shape reads `That does not look like a DigitalOcean personal access token.`; a well-formed token DigitalOcean rejects shows its HTTP error (`401 Unauthorized`). Back returns to the Providers tab.

signed in, the panel lists the team's OpenHands agents and their sessions, **New Agent** (name and sandbox size), refresh and sign-out; connecting a session (or **Resume and connect** a paused one) adds it as the active backend, the sidebar's conversation list becomes that agent's session panel (`mars-session-panel`), and Manage Backends' Managed Agents view offers Pause, Stop, Disconnect and Open per session (blocked: needs a DigitalOcean account with Managed Agents).
removing a DigitalOcean backend in Manage Backends explains that it only disconnects and offers **Disconnect only** or **Stop session** (blocked: needs a connected DigitalOcean session).
a Canvas served with `--lock-to-cloud <url>` shows only the Cloud login (no close) on first run, and its selector footer reads **Reconnect to Cloud** with no add, edit or remove.

scenarios.name: F25--open-the-selector
scenarios.title: Open the selector
scenarios.body: From `/conversations` run `control-openhands browser click 'testid=backend-selector'` and `control-openhands browser snapshot 'testid=backend-selector'`. The snapshot shows `listbox` with `option "Connected Local"`, a separator, `button "Add Backend"` and `button "Manage Backends"`. Screenshot with `control-openhands browser screenshot --feature F25.selector-dropdown --name open`. Hover opens it too: `browser press Escape`, move the pointer away with `control-openhands browser hover 'testid=command-menu-trigger'` (hovering a selector the pointer is already on does nothing), `control-openhands browser hover 'testid=backend-selector'`, then the same snapshot shows `combobox "Local" [expanded]` and the two footer buttons.
scenarios.raw: **Open the selector (`F25.selector-dropdown`).** From `/conversations` run `control-openhands browser click 'testid=backend-selector'` and `control-openhands browser snapshot 'testid=backend-selector'`. The snapshot shows `listbox` with `option "Connected Local"`, a separator, `button "Add Backend"` and `button "Manage Backends"`. Screenshot with `control-openhands browser screenshot --feature F25.selector-dropdown --name open`. Hover opens it too: `browser press Escape`, move the pointer away with `control-openhands browser hover 'testid=command-menu-trigger'` (hovering a selector the pointer is already on does nothing), `control-openhands browser hover 'testid=backend-selector'`, then the same snapshot shows `combobox "Local" [expanded]` and the two footer buttons.
expected: clicking (or hovering) the selector opens a listbox of backends, each option named `<status> <name>` with a status dot, and a footer with **Add Backend** and **Manage Backends**.
notes:
Expected: Escape never clears the backend selector. Known failure (reproduced 2026-10-09, 2026-10-12, 2026-10-13 and 2026-10-14, [#18233](https://github.com/OpenHands/OpenHands/issues/18233)): Escape on the focused backend selector while its menu is closed (a second Escape after the one that closes the menu, and sometimes the Escape that closes Manage Backends opened from it) clears the selection: the closed selector shows the active backend's name as an italic placeholder (`browser value 'testid=backend-selector >> role=combobox'` is `""`) and its status dot is gone, so `browser wait 'testid=backend-selector >> role=status[name="Disconnected"]'` times out although the backend is down; a reload restores it. Reload before a closed-selector status check, as the Edit bullet does. Repro: `browser click 'testid=backend-selector'`, `browser press Escape` twice ([#18233](https://github.com/OpenHands/OpenHands/issues/18233)). On 2026-10-12 `bug proof` verified fix PR #18238 at 77de0ad24 against main f07aebdf5 (two `xfail`, two `xpass`, desktop). `control-openhands bug run F25.selector-dropdown` replays it (desktop, after a reload with the mouse off the selector: a reload under a mouse left on it opens its menu and empties its field, which would look like the bug) and reports `xfail` while the bug lasts:

  ```sh known-bug F25.selector-dropdown escape-closed
  control-openhands browser viewport desktop
  control-openhands browser goto /
  control-openhands browser hover 'testid=root-layout'
  control-openhands browser reload
  control-openhands browser wait 'testid=backend-selector >> role=status[name="Connected"]' --timeout 15000
  control-openhands assert --field value --equals Local -- browser value 'testid=backend-selector >> role=combobox'
  control-openhands browser click 'testid=backend-selector'
  control-openhands browser press Escape
  control-openhands browser press Escape
  control-openhands browser screenshot 'testid=backend-selector' --feature F25.selector-dropdown --name escape-closed
  control-openhands assert --field value --equals Local --bug-shows '' -- browser value 'testid=backend-selector >> role=combobox'  # bug
  ```

scenarios.name: F25--switch-with-the-overlay

scenarios.name: F25--per-tab-backend
scenarios.title: Per-tab backend
scenarios.body: With `Local` active and `QA_Second` registered, run `control-openhands browser goto /conversations` and `control-openhands browser eval "JSON.parse(sessionStorage.getItem('openhands-active-backend')).backendId"` (`default-local`); note QA_Second's id with `control-openhands browser eval "JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem('openhands-backends')).find(b=>b.name==='QA_Second').id"` (`<second-id>`, a generated UUID). Open a plain second tab, as a user opening the app again: `control-openhands browser tab new /conversations` prints `index` `1` and makes it the daemon's active tab (`control-openhands browser tabs` lists two pages at `/conversations` with `active` `1`); `control-openhands browser wait-tab '/conversations$' --new --timeout 5000` then prints `index` `0`, the tab you came from, because `--new` leaves out the tab the daemon is on and that is now the new one (run from `browser tab 0` it prints `index` `1`, the second tab). `control-openhands browser tab 1`, `control-openhands browser wait 'testid=backend-selector'`: `browser snapshot 'testid=backend-selector'` reads `combobox "Local"` and `control-openhands browser eval "sessionStorage.getItem('openhands-active-backend')"` is `null` (a new tab inherits nothing and starts from the localStorage fallback). Switch this tab: `browser click 'testid=backend-selector'`, `control-openhands browser click 'testid=backend-selector >> role=option[name="Connected QA_Second"]'`, `control-openhands browser wait 'testid=environment-switch-overlay' --state detached --timeout 10000`; the selector reads `QA_Second`, `browser count 'testid=conversation-card'` is `0` and `control-openhands browser eval "JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem('openhands-active-backend')).backendId"` is `<second-id>`. Back in `control-openhands browser tab 0` nothing moved: the selector still reads `Local`, the card count is `1`, the sessionStorage eval is still `default-local` while the localStorage eval is `<second-id>` (`browser screenshot --feature F25.per-tab-backend --name first-tab-unchanged`). A plain new tab starts from the last choice made in any tab: from tab 0 run `control-openhands browser tab new /conversations` (`index` `2`, now active), `browser wait 'testid=backend-selector'`: the selector reads `QA_Second`, the card count is `0`, its sessionStorage item is `null` and the localStorage eval is `<second-id>` (`--name plain-new-tab-last-choice`). A conversation row opens on its owner instead: `control-openhands browser tab 0`, `control-openhands browser click 'testid=conversation-card' --modifiers Control` (add `>> nth=0` when the run holds more conversations than the precondition's one: the click is strict), `control-openhands browser wait-tab '/conversations/<id>' --timeout 20000` prints `index` `3` and the URL `/conversations/<id>?backend=default-local`; `control-openhands browser tab 3`, `control-openhands browser wait 'testid=chat-interface' --timeout 30000`, `browser url` still ends in `/conversations/<id>?backend=default-local` (no bounce to `/conversations`), the selector reads `Local` and `browser toasts --history` lists only `Loading...` (no `This conversation does not exist…`); `browser screenshot --feature F25.per-tab-backend --name new-tab-on-owner`. Close the extra tabs highest first: `control-openhands browser close-tab 3`, `control-openhands browser close-tab 2`, `control-openhands browser close-tab 1`, `control-openhands browser tab 0`; `browser tabs` lists one page and the selector reads `Local`. Opening the pinned link also recorded `default-local` as the last choice (the localStorage eval in tab 3 reads `default-local`), so run the plain-new-tab check before the row check.

scenarios.name: F25--health-status
scenarios.title: Health status
scenarios.body: With QA_Renamed the active backend (as the Edit bullet's reload leaves it; the closed selector shows only the active backend's dot), run `control-openhands service stop agent-server --run "$OH_VERIFY_RUN_2"`, then on the open page `control-openhands browser wait 'testid=backend-selector >> role=status[name="Disconnected"]' --timeout 40000`. `browser click 'testid=backend-selector'` and `browser snapshot 'testid=backend-selector'` show `option "Disconnected QA_Renamed"` next to `option "Connected Local"`. In Manage Backends `browser text 'testid=manage-backends-status-QA_Renamed'` is `Disconnected (check URL or network)`, `testid=manage-backends-status-detail-QA_Renamed` repeats it with `Check that the backend URL is correct ...`, and `browser enabled 'testid=manage-backends-row-QA_Renamed >> role=button >> nth=0'` is `false`. An error toast with the same text also appears. Screenshot with `--feature F25.health-status --name manage-down`.
scenarios.raw: **Health status (`F25.health-status`).** With QA_Renamed the active backend (as the Edit bullet's reload leaves it; the closed selector shows only the active backend's dot), run `control-openhands service stop agent-server --run "$OH_VERIFY_RUN_2"`, then on the open page `control-openhands browser wait 'testid=backend-selector >> role=status[name="Disconnected"]' --timeout 40000`. `browser click 'testid=backend-selector'` and `browser snapshot 'testid=backend-selector'` show `option "Disconnected QA_Renamed"` next to `option "Connected Local"`. In Manage Backends `browser text 'testid=manage-backends-status-QA_Renamed'` is `Disconnected (check URL or network)`, `testid=manage-backends-status-detail-QA_Renamed` repeats it with `Check that the backend URL is correct ...`, and `browser enabled 'testid=manage-backends-row-QA_Renamed >> role=button >> nth=0'` is `false`. An error toast with the same text also appears. Screenshot with `--feature F25.health-status --name manage-down`.
expected: a backend that stops answering turns its dot red (`Disconnected`) within one health probe (every 30 s for local and remote agent servers; Cloud backends every 5 min and not on window focus or reconnect, #18128); its Manage row reads `Disconnected (check URL or network)` with a red detail line and cannot be selected.
notes: Known issue [#15822](https://github.com/OpenHands/OpenHands/issues/15822) (`F25.switch-backend` `F25.health-status` `F25.cloud-org-rows`): Cloud-proxy traffic was reported to continue after switching from Cloud to Local. Current source probes registered inactive Cloud backends on a five-minute cadence; recheck the reported repeated OPTIONS behavior with a real registered Cloud account/org and capture only credential-redacted request metadata after switching. This run has no authenticated Cloud backend.

Known issue [OpenHands/software-agent-sdk#5789](https://github.com/OpenHands/software-agent-sdk/issues/5789) (`F25.add-agent-server`, `F25.health-status`): a deferred-init Agent Server can report ready after accepting a GUI origin through `/api/init`, while browser preflights from that origin still fail and Canvas cannot connect. Recheck an owned warm-pool server initialized with the actual non-localhost Canvas origin and compare admission with an origin supplied at server boot. The default loopback-origin stack is already allowed and cannot exercise this branch.

scenarios.name: F25--recovery-gate
scenarios.title: Recovery gate
scenarios.body: Close the modal, `control-openhands browser reload`, then `control-openhands browser wait 'testid=manage-backends-modal' --timeout 20000`. `browser testids` lists `agent-server-onboarding-screen` and the Manage rows but no sidebar; `browser count 'testid=close-manage-backends-modal'` and `browser count 'testid=manage-backends-done'` are `0`, and `browser press Escape` leaves the modal (`count` `1`). `control-openhands browser click 'testid=manage-backends-row-Local >> role=button >> nth=0'` and `browser wait 'testid=agent-server-onboarding-screen' --state detached --timeout 15000` restore the app: selector `Local`, card count `1`. Screenshot the gate with `--feature F25.recovery-gate --name gate` before choosing.
scenarios.raw: **Recovery gate (`F25.recovery-gate`).** Close the modal, `control-openhands browser reload`, then `control-openhands browser wait 'testid=manage-backends-modal' --timeout 20000`. `browser testids` lists `agent-server-onboarding-screen` and the Manage rows but no sidebar; `browser count 'testid=close-manage-backends-modal'` and `browser count 'testid=manage-backends-done'` are `0`, and `browser press Escape` leaves the modal (`count` `1`). `control-openhands browser click 'testid=manage-backends-row-Local >> role=button >> nth=0'` and `browser wait 'testid=agent-server-onboarding-screen' --state detached --timeout 15000` restore the app: selector `Local`, card count `1`. Screenshot the gate with `--feature F25.recovery-gate --name gate` before choosing.
expected: reloading while the active backend is down shows only `agent-server-onboarding-screen` with Manage backends in recovery mode (no X, no Done, Escape ignored, primary **Add Backend**); choosing a healthy row restores the app.

scenarios.name: F25--remove-the-active-backend
scenarios.title: Remove the active backend
scenarios.body: Run `control-openhands restart --run "$OH_VERIFY_RUN_2"`, `browser click 'testid=backend-selector'`, `browser wait 'testid=backend-selector >> role=option[name="Connected QA_Renamed"]' --timeout 25000` and click that option (selector reads `QA_Renamed`). Open Manage Backends, `control-openhands browser click 'testid=manage-backends-remove-QA_Renamed'`; `browser text 'testid=confirmation-modal'` reads `Remove backend "QA_Renamed"? If it is active, the app will switch back to Local.` `control-openhands browser click 'testid=confirmation-modal >> role=button[name="Cancel"]'` keeps the row (`count 'testid=manage-backends-row-QA_Renamed'` `1`). Click the trash again, then `control-openhands browser click 'testid=confirmation-modal >> testid=confirm-button'`: the row count is `0`. Click Done and `browser reload`: the selector reads `Local`, `browser count 'testid=backend-selector >> role=option'` (dropdown open) is `1`, and the card count is `1`.
scenarios.raw: **Remove the active backend (`F25.remove-backend`).** Run `control-openhands restart --run "$OH_VERIFY_RUN_2"`, `browser click 'testid=backend-selector'`, `browser wait 'testid=backend-selector >> role=option[name="Connected QA_Renamed"]' --timeout 25000` and click that option (selector reads `QA_Renamed`). Open Manage Backends, `control-openhands browser click 'testid=manage-backends-remove-QA_Renamed'`; `browser text 'testid=confirmation-modal'` reads `Remove backend "QA_Renamed"? If it is active, the app will switch back to Local.` `control-openhands browser click 'testid=confirmation-modal >> role=button[name="Cancel"]'` keeps the row (`count 'testid=manage-backends-row-QA_Renamed'` `1`). Click the trash again, then `control-openhands browser click 'testid=confirmation-modal >> testid=confirm-button'`: the row count is `0`. Click Done and `browser reload`: the selector reads `Local`, `browser count 'testid=backend-selector >> role=option'` (dropdown open) is `1`, and the card count is `1`.
expected: the trash icon asks `Remove backend "<name>"? If it is active, the app will switch back to Local.`; Cancel keeps it, Confirm removes it and an active removed backend falls back to Local (BM-003).

scenarios.name: F25--add-from-manage-edit-cancel-and-x
scenarios.title: Add from Manage, Edit Cancel and X
scenarios.body: The second stack is running again after the previous bullet. Run `browser goto /conversations/<id>`, `browser wait 'testid=chat-interface'`, open the selector, click `manage-backends-menu-item`, then `control-openhands browser click 'testid=manage-backends-add'` and `control-openhands browser wait 'testid=add-backend-modal' --timeout 5000` (`visible`); `browser count 'testid=manage-backends-modal'` is `1` underneath. `browser click 'testid=add-backend-close'`: the Add count is `0` and the Manage count stays `1`. Click `manage-backends-add` again, `add-backend-option-agent-server`, fill `add-backend-name` with `QA_Second`, `add-backend-host` with `<second-url>` and `add-backend-api-key` with `--value-file "$OH_VERIFY_RUN_2/private/session-key"`, then `browser click 'testid=add-backend-submit' --expect-url '/conversations(\?|$)'`: the URL is `/conversations`, `count 'testid=add-backend-modal'` is `0`, `count 'testid=manage-backends-modal'` is still `1`, `count 'testid=manage-backends-row-QA_Second'` is `1` and the selector reads `QA_Second` (screenshot `--feature F25.manage-add --name after-add`). No consent prompt this time: it is stored on the second backend. Then `control-openhands browser click 'testid=manage-backends-edit-QA_Second'`, `browser fill 'testid=edit-backend-name' QA_Draft` and `control-openhands browser click 'testid=edit-backend-cancel'`: `count 'testid=edit-backend-modal'` `0`, `count 'testid=manage-backends-modal'` `1`, row `QA_Second` `1`, row `QA_Draft` `0`. Repeat with `control-openhands browser click 'testid=edit-backend-close'`: same counts, and reopening the pencil shows `browser value 'testid=edit-backend-name'` `QA_Second`; leave with `edit-backend-cancel`. Remove it again: `browser click 'testid=manage-backends-remove-QA_Second'`, `browser click 'testid=confirmation-modal >> testid=confirm-button'`, `browser click 'testid=manage-backends-done'` and `browser reload`: the selector reads `Local`.
scenarios.raw: **Add from Manage, Edit Cancel and X (`F25.manage-add`, `F25.edit-cancel`).** The second stack is running again after the previous bullet. Run `browser goto /conversations/<id>`, `browser wait 'testid=chat-interface'`, open the selector, click `manage-backends-menu-item`, then `control-openhands browser click 'testid=manage-backends-add'` and `control-openhands browser wait 'testid=add-backend-modal' --timeout 5000` (`visible`); `browser count 'testid=manage-backends-modal'` is `1` underneath. `browser click 'testid=add-backend-close'`: the Add count is `0` and the Manage count stays `1`. Click `manage-backends-add` again, `add-backend-option-agent-server`, fill `add-backend-name` with `QA_Second`, `add-backend-host` with `<second-url>` and `add-backend-api-key` with `--value-file "$OH_VERIFY_RUN_2/private/session-key"`, then `browser click 'testid=add-backend-submit' --expect-url '/conversations(\?|$)'`: the URL is `/conversations`, `count 'testid=add-backend-modal'` is `0`, `count 'testid=manage-backends-modal'` is still `1`, `count 'testid=manage-backends-row-QA_Second'` is `1` and the selector reads `QA_Second` (screenshot `--feature F25.manage-add --name after-add`). No consent prompt this time: it is stored on the second backend. Then `control-openhands browser click 'testid=manage-backends-edit-QA_Second'`, `browser fill 'testid=edit-backend-name' QA_Draft` and `control-openhands browser click 'testid=edit-backend-cancel'`: `count 'testid=edit-backend-modal'` `0`, `count 'testid=manage-backends-modal'` `1`, row `QA_Second` `1`, row `QA_Draft` `0`. Repeat with `control-openhands browser click 'testid=edit-backend-close'`: same counts, and reopening the pencil shows `browser value 'testid=edit-backend-name'` `QA_Second`; leave with `edit-backend-cancel`. Remove it again: `browser click 'testid=manage-backends-remove-QA_Second'`, `browser click 'testid=confirmation-modal >> testid=confirm-button'`, `browser click 'testid=manage-backends-done'` and `browser reload`: the selector reads `Local`.
expected: **Add Backend** in Manage backends opens the same Add form stacked over Manage; its X returns to Manage, and a successful add keeps Manage open with the new row while the new backend becomes active.
**Cancel** and the X in Edit backend close only the Edit modal and discard the draft; Manage backends stays open with the stored values.
notes: Known failure (repro candidate, not an exemption): `F25.edit-escape` closes the Manage modal underneath and drops the Edit draft (Cancel and X close only Edit, `F25.edit-cancel`) ([#17953](https://github.com/OpenHands/OpenHands/issues/17953)).

scenarios.name: F25--collapsed-rail

scenarios.body: Run `control-openhands browser click 'testid=sidebar-collapse-toggle'` (`attr 'aside[data-collapsed]' data-collapsed` is `true`), `control-openhands browser hover 'testid=collapsed-backend-selector-link'`, `control-openhands browser click 'testid=add-backend-menu-item'` and `control-openhands browser wait 'testid=add-backend-modal' --timeout 5000` (`visible`). scenarios.raw: **Collapsed rail (`F25.collapsed-entry`).** Run `control-openhands browser click 'testid=sidebar-collapse-toggle'` (`attr 'aside[data-collapsed]' data-collapsed` is `true`), `control-openhands browser hover 'testid=collapsed-backend-selector-link'`, `control-openhands browser click 'testid=add-backend-menu-item'` and `control-openhands browser wait 'testid=add-backend-modal' --timeout 5000` (`visible`). Close it (the drawer stays open), open Manage Backends from the drawer selector the same way and check `bbox 'testid=manage-backends-modal'` the same. scenarios.name: F25--providers-tab
scenarios.title: Providers tab
scenarios.body: On the default run `browser eval "!!window.marsBridge"` is `true` (Preconditions); `curl -s "http://127.0.0.1:$(control-openhands status | jq -r .ports.frontend)/mars/health"` (the static child behind the ingress) returns the HTML index, not JSON: one bridge per stack. Open Add Backend: the tablist adds `tab "Providers Connect through DigitalOcean and more."` (`testid=add-backend-option-providers`); `control-openhands browser click 'testid=add-backend-option-providers'` and `browser snapshot 'testid=add-backend-providers-panel'` show `button "DigitalOcean Your team's OpenHands agents"` and `More providers coming soon.` (`browser screenshot --feature F25.add-backend-modal --name with-providers-tab`). At phone width the modal stays inside the viewport with the three tab titles cut to `Ope…`, `Age…`, `Pro…` (`--feature F25.providers-tab --name phone-tabs`).
scenarios.raw: **Providers tab (`F25.providers-tab`).** On the default run `browser eval "!!window.marsBridge"` is `true` (Preconditions); `curl -s "http://127.0.0.1:$(control-openhands status | jq -r .ports.frontend)/mars/health"` (the static child behind the ingress) returns the HTML index, not JSON: one bridge per stack. Open Add Backend: the tablist adds `tab "Providers Connect through DigitalOcean and more."` (`testid=add-backend-option-providers`); `control-openhands browser click 'testid=add-backend-option-providers'` and `browser snapshot 'testid=add-backend-providers-panel'` show `button "DigitalOcean Your team's OpenHands agents"` and `More providers coming soon.` (`browser screenshot --feature F25.add-backend-modal --name with-providers-tab`). At phone width the modal stays inside the viewport with the three tab titles cut to `Ope…`, `Age…`, `Pro…` (`--feature F25.providers-tab --name phone-tabs`).
expected: only when the page has the Managed Agents bridge (`window.marsBridge`), Add Backend shows a third tab **Providers** ("Connect through DigitalOcean and more.") with a **DigitalOcean** card ("Your team's OpenHands agents") and `More providers coming soon.`. Every launcher-served web page has it (the ingress answers `/mars/health`); without it (`MARS_WEB=0`, or a non-loopback bind with no session key at all) there are only the Cloud and Agent-server tabs and no Managed Agents UI anywhere. A non-loopback bind that has a key (F26 `--host 0.0.0.0` with `LOCAL_BACKEND_API_KEY`) mounts the bridge behind that key and offers the tab too, although the page itself carries no key (see the sign-in bullet's
annotations: Known failure).

scenarios.name: F25--digitalocean-sign-in
scenarios.title: DigitalOcean sign-in
scenarios.body: On the default run, run `control-openhands browser click 'testid=add-backend-provider-digitalocean'` and `browser wait 'testid=managed-agents-sign-in'`: heading `Connect your DigitalOcean team`, `textbox "Personal access token"` (`browser attr 'testid=managed-agents-token' type` is `password`), link `Create a token` (`/url: https://cloud.digitalocean.com/account/api/tokens`) and `button "Connect with token" [disabled]`; no OAuth button in a browser (`browser count 'testid=managed-agents-oauth'` is `0`). Fill `testid=managed-agents-token` with `dop_v1_qa_invalid_token_0000` and click `testid=managed-agents-token-submit`: `browser text 'testid=managed-agents-auth-error'` reads `That does not look like a DigitalOcean personal access token.` (`POST /mars/rpc/savePat` `500`). Fill a well-formed dummy, `dop_v1_` plus 64 zeros, and submit again: after a few seconds the error reads `401 Unauthorized` (`POST /mars/rpc/savePat` `401`, DigitalOcean's answer; `browser screenshot --feature F25.digitalocean-sign-in --name rejected-token`). Never type a real token here. `control-openhands browser click 'testid=add-backend-providers-back'` returns to the Providers panel (`browser count 'testid=managed-agents-sign-in'` is `0`; the providers panel itself stays mounted behind the sign-in screen, so its count is `1` either way); close with `testid=add-backend-close`. At phone width the sign-in screen fits (`bbox 'testid=add-backend-modal'` `insideViewport` `true`). Both errors also raise an error toast with the same text. Expected on a page served without a baked key (F26 `--host 0.0.0.0`, Docker), once the server's key was typed on the API-key screen: the same two answers as above. Known failure (reproduced 2026-10-14, #18434): every token, even the malformed one, ends in `session key required` (`POST /mars/rpc/getAuthState` and `savePat` `401`), because the web bridge client sends only the baked page key, never the typed one; it predates #18349 (BASE with `MARS_WEB=1` fails the same way). A `--frontend-only` page connected to another stack's backend fails the same way for a different reason (the typed key belongs to the other stack); #18434 leaves that case to a maintainer decision.

Fill `testid=managed-agents-token` with `dop_v1_qa_invalid_token_0000` and click `testid=managed-agents-token-submit`: `browser text 'testid=managed-agents-auth-error'` reads `That does not look like a DigitalOcean personal access token.` (`POST /mars/rpc/savePat` `500`). Fill a well-formed dummy, `dop_v1_` plus 64 zeros, and submit again: after a few seconds the error reads `401 Unauthorized` (`POST /mars/rpc/savePat` `401`, DigitalOcean's answer; `browser screenshot --feature F25.digitalocean-sign-in --name rejected-token`). Never type a real token here. `control-openhands browser click 'testid=add-backend-providers-back'` returns to the Providers panel (`browser count 'testid=managed-agents-sign-in'` is `0`; the providers panel itself stays mounted behind the sign-in screen, so its count is `1` either way); close with `testid=add-backend-close`. At phone width the sign-in screen fits (`bbox 'testid=add-backend-modal'` `insideViewport` `true`). Both errors also raise an error toast with the same text. Expected on a page served without a baked key (F26 `--host 0.0.0.0`, Docker), once the server's key was typed on the API-key screen: the same two answers as above. Known failure (reproduced 2026-10-14, #18434): every token, even the malformed one, ends in `session key required` (`POST /mars/rpc/getAuthState` and `savePat` `401`), because the web bridge client sends only the baked page key, never the typed one; it predates #18349 (BASE with `MARS_WEB=1` fails the same way). scenarios.name: F25--managed-agents-with-an-account
scenarios.title: Managed Agents with an account
scenarios.body: Blocked: needs a DigitalOcean account with Managed Agents. With one, after a real token the panel lists agents (`digitalocean-agent-<id>`), **New Agent** opens `digitalocean-new-agent-form` (name, size), a session's Connect adds a backend and the sidebar shows `mars-session-panel`; removing that backend opens `mars-backend-removal-modal` with `disconnect-only-button` and `stop-session-button`.
scenarios.raw: **Managed Agents with an account (`F25.digitalocean-agents`, `F25.digitalocean-backend-removal`).** Blocked: needs a DigitalOcean account with Managed Agents. With one, after a real token the panel lists agents (`digitalocean-agent-<id>`), **New Agent** opens `digitalocean-new-agent-form` (name, size), a session's Connect adds a backend and the sidebar shows `mars-session-panel`; removing that backend opens `mars-backend-removal-modal` with `disconnect-only-button` and `stop-session-button`.
expected: signed in, the panel lists the team's OpenHands agents and their sessions, **New Agent** (name and sandbox size), refresh and sign-out; connecting a session (or **Resume and connect** a paused one) adds it as the active backend, the sidebar's conversation list becomes that agent's session panel (`mars-session-panel`), and Manage Backends' Managed Agents view offers Pause, Stop, Disconnect and Open per session (blocked: needs a DigitalOcean account with Managed Agents).
removing a DigitalOcean backend in Manage Backends explains that it only disconnects and offers **Disconnect only** or **Stop session** (blocked: needs a connected DigitalOcean session).

scenarios.name: F25--cloud-backend
scenarios.title: Cloud backend
scenarios.body: Only with a Cloud account (Preconditions); it creates a device grant and one conversation on that account, and shows the account's own conversations in the sidebar (keep those screenshots private). Reopen Add Backend on the Cloud tab, `browser click 'testid=add-backend-login-button'`, then `control-openhands browser tab 1` (the verify popup: `Device Authorization Request`, the code, **Authorize Device**), `control-openhands browser click 'role=button[name="Authorize Device"]'` (`Success!`) and `control-openhands browser tab 0`. Within about 15 s (token polling answers `400` until approved, then `200`) `browser count 'testid=add-backend-modal'` is `0`, the popup is gone and `browser snapshot 'testid=backend-selector'` reads `combobox "OpenHands Cloud": OpenHands Cloud – Personal Workspace`; the registry holds `{name: "OpenHands Cloud", host: "https://app.all-hands.dev", kind: "cloud"}` (`browser eval "JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem('openhands-backends')).map(b=>({name:b.name,host:b.host,kind:b.kind}))"`).
