families.title: Launcher modes, Docker, desktop and library
families.overview:
Agent Canvas ships one UI in several runtime shapes. The npm launcher
(`npx @openhands/agent-canvas`, here `node bin/agent-canvas.mjs`) runs the full
stack, or only the frontend or only the backends, prints its version and stack
info, refuses conflicting flags, and decides whether the session key is
injected into the page (loopback) or the user must paste it (`--public`, or a
non-loopback `--host`). The same stack also ships as a Docker image, an
Electron desktop app and an embeddable React library. Launchers tell the agent
which services exist through `/server_info.runtime_services` and a
`<RUNTIME_SERVICES>` block in every new conversation's system prompt.
families.entry:
- A terminal: `npx @openhands/agent-canvas [flags]`; from this checkout, `node bin/agent-canvas.mjs [flags]` (what `control-openhands launch` starts with `--port`, and `--public` for public mode).
- The browser at the ingress URL the launcher prints (`http://localhost:8000/` by default).
- Backend selector (`backend-selector`) → **Add Backend** (`add-backend-menu-item`) → **Agent-server** → **Remote**, and **Manage Backends** to remove it (see F25 for the backend registry itself).
- Public mode and the API-key screen are mapped in F01 (`F01.api-key-entry`, `F01.onboarding-backend-step`).
- `npm run build:lib` for the embeddable library; a host app imports `@openhands/agent-canvas` (see `docs/DEVELOPMENT.md`, "Cloud organization recovery in embedded hosts").
- `docker run ... ghcr.io/openhands/agent-canvas` or `npm run build:docker`, then `http://localhost:8000/canvas`.
- `helm install agent-canvas ./helm/agent-canvas` on a Kubernetes cluster (`helm/agent-canvas/README.md`).
- `npm run desktop` (development) or a packaged build from `npm run build:desktop`; the window opens itself.
- ACP agents (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI) are chosen in onboarding (F01) and Settings → Agents (F13); this family does not repeat them.
families.given:
Preconditions:

- Baseline state (launched, doctored, `onboard --skip` done) on your own run: `control-openhands launch --new --build never`, `export OH_VERIFY_RUN=<run from the launch JSON>`, `control-openhands doctor`, `control-openhands onboard --skip`. Commands run from the checkout root.
- `F26.desktop-*` need the Electron binary (`node_modules/electron/dist/electron`; `npx --no-install electron --version` downloads it on first use) and `Xvfb` plus ImageMagick `import` for headless capture. The app binds the fixed ports 8000, 18000, 18001 and 3001: check them like the blocks below and keep the run short.
- `F26.runtime-services` and `F26.runtime-services-agent-use` need an active LLM profile (`control-openhands llm preset deepseek`); the second also needs the automation service running and costs two short runs (the conversation and the dispatched automation run).
- The partial-stack and LAN bullets start extra launchers by hand (harness gap: `launch` has no `--frontend-only`, `--backend-only` or `--host`). Each one needs a free block of ports: these recipes use 18960–18963 and 18970–18973, plus 19961, the editor port a launcher that serves VS Code hands its agent-server (see Gotchas); check them first with `for p in 18960 18961 18962 18963 18970 18971 18972 18973 19961; do (echo > /dev/tcp/127.0.0.1/$p) 2>/dev/null && echo "$p busy"; done` (no output means free). Each launcher gets a private `HOME` and state under `$OH_VERIFY_RUN/private/`, so it never touches `~/.openhands` or your run.
families.gotchas:
- `control-openhands launch` covers only the full stack and `--public`. Partial stacks and `--host` need a hand-started launcher with its own `HOME`, `OH_CANVAS_SAFE_STATE_DIR` and all three `OH_CANVAS_SAFE_*_PORT` variables; without them it writes into the real `~/.openhands/agent-canvas` and grabs the default ports 8000/18000/18001/3001 that another agent may be using.
- A hand-started launcher's first start downloads the agent-server into its private `HOME` cache (30–90 s). Prefix assignments are expanded left to right, so `HOME=$Q/home UV_CACHE_DIR=$HOME/.cache/uv` points the cache into `$Q/home` too, not at your real cache. Reuse one `$Q` for repeat launches to keep it warm.
- The browser daemon refuses other origins unless you pass `--allow-external` to `browser goto`. Each port is its own origin, so a partial-stack page starts at first run again (onboarding and a consent dialog), independent of your run's onboarding.
- In a frontend-only UI the **Add a backend** step's Next is enabled with an empty key, while on a LAN or `--public` stack it is disabled until a key is typed: the host the step probes differs (503 vs. auth-required).
- A partial-stack origin keeps its stored backend in the browser profile across launches, so a second pass lands straight in the shell. `control-openhands browser reset` brings back the first run on every origin; then `control-openhands browser goto /` and `control-openhands onboard --skip` restore your own run's baseline.
- Which screen a frontend-only origin shows depends on the browser, not the launcher: a profile new to the origin gets **Add a backend** (first run owns the initial backend), while a profile that stores a backend for that origin (the `default-local` entry a full launcher on the same port seeded, or any backend added there earlier) gets the recovery gate of `F25.recovery-gate` as soon as that backend answers 503 (`F26.frontend-only-returning`). The no-toast check belongs to the first-run state only: on the gate, `browser toasts --history` lists generic `An error occurred` status toasts raised by the failing 503 probes (two within 12 s here), with no hint of which request failed. Known failure (reproduced 2026-10-08): both toasts come from the free-models hydrator's `GET /api/llm/models/verified` 503, which no `meta.disableToast` guards on that screen (nor does `backend-version.tsx`); [#18160](https://github.com/OpenHands/OpenHands/issues/18160).
- Stopping a backend-only instance while the frontend-only page that uses it stays open is the same backend-down state as `F25.recovery-gate` after a reload; keep the returning-user bullet above as the frontend-only-specific check (it reproduces the `default-local` case).
- The launcher serves the bundled VS Code editor. #17660 made that opt-in (`OH_CANVAS_ENABLE_VSCODE=true`) and #18048 reverted it, so only a checkout between the two needs the variable (`launch --vscode` sets it). A launcher that serves it reserves `/vscode/`: a frontend-only stack answers `503` there and logs `[static] /vscode -> 503 (rejected)`; a stack with an agent-server lists `/vscode → http://127.0.0.1:<agent-server port + 1000>` in its ingress banner and hands the agent-server that editor port (19961 for the hand-started launchers here, 19000 for the desktop app), which the launcher's own port check does not cover. On a checkout between the two without the variable, `/vscode/` is an ordinary SPA URL (`200`). Here the agent-server has no editor binary (`VSCode server binary not found, VSCode will be disabled` in the launcher log, `/api/vscode/status` `{"running":false,"enabled":true}`), so the editor port stays free even then.
- The port-in-use error is printed twice, the second time with a Node stack trace, and suggests `PORT=<other>` rather than `--port` ([#17949](https://github.com/OpenHands/OpenHands/issues/17949)). The `--public` key error's example says `npm run dev -- --public` instead of the npx command.
- A backend-only instance's `/server_info.runtime_services` still describes the ingress as routing `/* to the frontend`, which it does not run ([#17949](https://github.com/OpenHands/OpenHands/issues/17949)).
- In this sandbox `node_modules/electron/dist` is absent and `node node_modules/electron/install.js` fails with `ERR_ASSERTION` (2026-10-13), so the `F26.desktop-*` rows stay blocked here.
- The Electron app hardcodes ports 8000/18000/18001 (and the static server takes 3001), ignores `PORT`, and refuses to start as root without `--no-sandbox` (`Running as root without --no-sandbox is not supported`). `npm run desktop` first runs `build:app`, which rebuilds `build/` under every other run: start `node_modules/.bin/electron --no-sandbox electron` directly against the existing build.
- Never stop the desktop app with one group-wide signal: when Xvfb dies with Electron, the app exits without stopping its backend, which is left orphaned (own process groups, parent 1) on 8000/18000/18001/3001 and blocks the next start. If that happens, find the orphans by their ports' command lines (`ps -eo pid,pgid,cmd`, look for `--port 18000`, `--port 18001`, `--port 3001`, `ingress.mjs --port 8000`) and stop each group by id.
- The generated session key lives in `$HOME/.openhands/agent-canvas/api-key.txt`, not under `OH_CANVAS_SAFE_STATE_DIR`: a hand-started launcher without a private `HOME` reads and writes the operator's real key file.
- A browser origin keeps the backends it stored on an earlier pass: after the LAN pass on 18960, a later loopback launch on 18960 shows the stale `QA_LAN` backend (red, old key) instead of onboarding, although the page injects a valid key. Assert key-injection bullets through the `window` globals, or `browser reset` first.
- Electron's splash shows each raw service-log line (`agent-server: {"asctime": ...`) as its status text during boot; the named phases only appear between them.
- `build:lib` from a copy whose `node_modules` is a symlink emits bundled dependencies under `dist/<absolute node_modules path>/...`; that path is an artifact of the copy, not of the product.
- **Bug candidate (`F26.host-bind-lan-optin`):** `scripts/bind-host.mjs` tells npm users to pass `--allow-lan-session-key`, but neither `bin/agent-canvas.mjs` nor `scripts/dev-with-automation.mjs` parses or forwards it (only `scripts/static-server.mjs` and the Docker entrypoint do), and unknown flags are silently ignored ([#17949](https://github.com/OpenHands/OpenHands/issues/17949), whose first item is exactly this; reproduced again on 2026-10-08 at d2c89252d).
- Known issue [#17946](https://github.com/OpenHands/OpenHands/issues/17946): the npm launcher never creates its `TMUX_TMPDIR`, so hand-started instances share one tmux server and a restart of one resets the others' terminals.
- Known issue [#17763](https://github.com/OpenHands/OpenHands/issues/17763) (`F26.docker-image`): The Docker entrypoint can leave protected Agent Server APIs unauthenticated when only `LOCAL_BACKEND_API_KEY` is supplied, because its export to `OH_SESSION_API_KEYS_0` is inside the generate-key branch. Recheck an owned container with a dummy custom key: unauthenticated `GET /api/conversations/search` must be 401 and the same request with that dummy key 200. `/server_info` is intentionally public and is not an auth probe. Blocked here without a Docker daemon.
- Known issue [#17623](https://github.com/OpenHands/OpenHands/issues/17623) (`F26.helm-chart`): The chart defaults service-account-token automounting to true even with RBAC disabled, exposing an unused cluster credential to agent processes. Recheck a disposable Kubernetes installation using the default values and an explicit opt-in; inspect token existence/readability only, never its contents. Blocked without Helm and a Kubernetes cluster.
- Known issue [#17470](https://github.com/OpenHands/OpenHands/issues/17470) (`F26.docker-image`): On Apple Silicon under Colima/Virtualization.framework, the image's Python services can exit with SIGILL while the frontend leaves onboarding at Disconnected. The report isolates `import litellm` and compares `OPENSSL_armcap=0`; recheck on the affected ARM/Colima guest with the reported cryptography/OpenSSL combination. A native macOS npm stack is not that container environment.
- Known issue [#17112](https://github.com/OpenHands/OpenHands/issues/17112) (`F26.desktop-main-window` `F26.desktop-external-links`): Desktop main-window navigation, an OAuth popup redirect, or a nested popup can render a remote page inside the app frame. Recheck all three on an owned running Electron shell with a harmless remote page and loopback redirect fixture; the browser harness cannot operate Electron windows and the installed Electron binary is unavailable here.
- Known issue [#16872](https://github.com/OpenHands/OpenHands/issues/16872) (`F26.desktop-external-links`): Non-browser URI schemes were reported to reach the OS handler from the desktop popup flow. Current source now parses hosts and restricts external protocols; recheck refusal in a running owned Electron shell before concluding resolution. Observe an inert denied test scheme without invoking any real OS handler. The browser harness cannot drive Electron and no installed Electron binary is available here.
- Known issue [#16774](https://github.com/OpenHands/OpenHands/issues/16774) (`F26.desktop-boot-splash` `F26.desktop-main-window`): The macOS 1.14.0 DMG installs an app that Gatekeeper reports as damaged instead of booting. Recheck the actual downloaded signed/notarized release artifact through install and first launch on macOS; starting source Electron or removing quarantine would bypass the reported failure. That release DMG/signature fixture is unavailable in this run.
- Known issue [#16720](https://github.com/OpenHands/OpenHands/issues/16720) (`F26.runtime-services`): CPU-heavy commands in several conversations can starve Agent Server and stop the UI loading; the report requests lower priority for agent commands than the service. Recheck with a disposable bounded workload, recorded CPU/resource limits and real command observations, never arbitrary stress on the shared machine. The exact Rust workload and affected resource envelope are missing, and real agent execution needs a model key. The backend counterpart is [OpenHands/software-agent-sdk#4575](https://github.com/OpenHands/software-agent-sdk/issues/4575).
- Known issue [#16690](https://github.com/OpenHands/OpenHands/issues/16690) (`F26.docker-image` `F26.runtime-services`): A Docker deployment with nine chats becomes slow/disconnected, then reloads lose the list and startup proxies report ECONNREFUSED. Recheck on the affected Windows-host Docker configuration with retained conversation state and a controlled workload; creating a few empty local chats cannot prove the reported resource/runtime failure. This run lacks Docker and the original conversation/workload fixture.
- Known issue [#16511](https://github.com/OpenHands/OpenHands/issues/16511) (`F26.docker-image`): The documented Docker bind mount can be unwritable to container uid 10001, killing Agent Server/automation while the frontend still serves Bad Gateway. Recheck a disposable host-owned mode-700 mount and a writable control against an owned image; never chmod the operator's real state directory. Blocked here without Docker.
- Known issue [#16300](https://github.com/OpenHands/OpenHands/issues/16300) (`F26.runtime-services`): The npm launcher can fail while building LiteLLM native dependencies when resolved AWS crates require a newer Rust compiler, leaving backend services unavailable. Recheck an isolated uncached uv environment with `litellm==1.95.0`, the reported Rust 1.93.1/toolchain/platform and dependency resolution; a warm current backend cache cannot exercise that install failure. The historical dependency/toolchain fixture is unavailable.
- Known issue [#16208](https://github.com/OpenHands/OpenHands/issues/16208) (`F26.runtime-services`): On Fedora Rawhide/Python 3.14.6, settings work but starting any conversation returns HTTP 500. Recheck a native Fedora environment with the reported SDK/runtime and model/profile, including the underlying server traceback; this macOS current-runtime stack cannot prove that platform-specific failure.
- Known issue [#15434](https://github.com/OpenHands/OpenHands/issues/15434) (`F26.remote-backend`): The embedded VS Code action on a self-hosted reverse-proxy origin was reported to reopen Canvas because its advertised URL omitted the separate editor port/path. Current launchers include an ingress `/vscode/` route; recheck against the affected HTTPS proxy deployment with an actually available editor binary and emitted URL before concluding resolution. This run lacks that self-hosted proxy/editor deployment.
- Known issue [OpenHands/software-agent-sdk#5373](https://github.com/OpenHands/software-agent-sdk/issues/5373) (`F26.remote-backend`): A self-hosted Agent Server using default Rich traceback logging can wedge its event loop and grow memory when a websocket error has a cyclic/deep exception chain; Canvas then times out or disconnects. The npm launcher forces JSON logging, so rechecking needs a separately hosted default-Rich backend plus the reported pathological peer/backlog reproducer and bounded memory/time isolation. That original peer/driver is not included in the issue body; do not synthesize a server patch or stress the shared host and claim a live UI reproduction.
- Known issue [OpenHands/software-agent-sdk#5310](https://github.com/OpenHands/software-agent-sdk/issues/5310) (`F26.docker-conversation-runtime`): A Docker conversation can lose the auxiliary title profile at the runtime boundary, leaving an ACP conversation untitled or producing an unrelated title-auth error while the agent still works. Recheck a saved reachable title profile and an ACP conversation inside an owned per-conversation Docker runtime, comparing its title/profile metadata with the host; inspect only profile names and credential-presence booleans. Blocked without Docker and real auxiliary-title/ACP credentials.
- Known issue [OpenHands/software-agent-sdk#5307](https://github.com/OpenHands/software-agent-sdk/issues/5307) (`F26.docker-conversation-runtime`): New worktree on a Docker-backed conversation can create git metadata whose reverse path exists only inside the container, so the still-live host worktree reads `prunable gitdir file points to non-existent location`. Recheck a disposable real git repository mounted into an owned conversation container, comparing host and container `git worktree list`/status while it is alive; a local worktree does not test the filesystem boundary. Blocked without Docker.
- Known issue [OpenHands/software-agent-sdk#4901](https://github.com/OpenHands/software-agent-sdk/issues/4901) (`F26.runtime-services`): closing an ACP conversation on POSIX is reported to leave the adapter's descendant Node/CLI processes alive after the top npm process exits. Recheck an owned authenticated ACP provider command chain, record its exact descendant identities before close and inspect only those identities afterwards; cleanup must target those owned groups. The current run has no authorized authenticated ACP runtime for this path.
- Known issue [OpenHands/software-agent-sdk#5974](https://github.com/OpenHands/software-agent-sdk/issues/5974) (`F26.runtime-services`; workspace picker in F03): a saved-workspace mutation waiting for its registry file lock can block the Agent Server event loop, including `/alive`, until the lock is released. Recheck only an owned registry using a bounded lock holder, an independently confirmed waiting mutation, concurrent liveness probes and a successful post-release readback; the original evidence uses Linux kernel lock-wait readback. A healthy idle server or concurrent writes without deliberate lock contention do not cover it.
- Known issue [OpenHands/software-agent-sdk#5731](https://github.com/OpenHands/software-agent-sdk/issues/5731) (`F26.cli-public-needs-key`): whitespace-only session keys remain configured credentials in the Agent Server. The Canvas launcher forwards a nonempty `LOCAL_BACKEND_API_KEY` verbatim, so a whitespace-only deployment value can leave the public login unable to use its intended key. Recheck an owned loopback-only public deployment with a whitespace-only supplied key, its actual HTTP/WebSocket authentication and a normal nonblank control; never test the server's default broad bind on an exposed interface. The SDK's missing-`OH_SECRET_KEY` cipher fallback is a separate configuration branch from a Canvas launcher that supplies an encryption key.

features.description: `--version` and `-v` print the package version and exit 0.
`--info` prints the package version, the default agent-server and automation pins, the minimum agent-server version, the default ports and the override env vars.
`--help` prints usage, auth modes, options, env vars and examples.
`--frontend-only` with `--backend-only`, and `--public` with `--frontend-only`, exit 1 with a one-line error before anything starts.
`--public` without `LOCAL_BACKEND_API_KEY` exits 1 with guidance.
a package without `build/` exits 1 with `No build found` and build instructions.
an occupied ingress (or service) port stops the launch with `Cannot start: the following ports are already in use` naming each busy port.
without `--host` the ingress listens on `127.0.0.1` only: the machine's own non-loopback address refuses the connection while loopback serves the app.

in local mode a stale session key left in the browser (the launcher's key changed since the last visit) is replaced by the injected key on load: the app opens on Home without the API-key screen, and the stored `Local` backend holds the new key (public mode asks for it instead: F01's api-key-entry row).
in local mode without `LOCAL_BACKEND_API_KEY` the launcher generates a session key, saves it under `$HOME/.openhands/agent-canvas/api-key.txt` and injects the same key again on the next start.
`LOCAL_BACKEND_API_KEY=<key>` in local mode injects exactly that key into the page and the API accepts only it (the saved generated key gets 401).

`--frontend-only` serves the SPA; `/server_info`, `/api/*`, `/sockets/*` and `/api/automation/*` answer 503, and a browser new to that origin opens on the **Add a backend** onboarding step without an error toast.

on a frontend-only origin, a browser that already stores a backend for that origin (the `default-local` entry a full launcher on the same port seeded, or one added there earlier) gets the recovery gate instead of onboarding: `agent-server-onboarding-screen` with Manage backends in recovery mode and the `Local` row `Disconnected` with the 503 detail (the gate itself is F25's recovery-gate row); the failing probes raise generic `An error occurred` toasts there (Known failure, reproduced 2026-10-08: [#18160](https://github.com/OpenHands/OpenHands/issues/18160)).
`--backend-only` serves the APIs (key-protected) and answers 503 `No backend configured for this route` for `/` and static assets.
a frontend-only UI connects to a separate backend-only instance through **Add a backend**; the shell then shows that backend as Connected and all API traffic goes to it.

from a normal Canvas, backend selector → **Add Backend** → **Agent-server** → **Remote** shows the self-hosting guidance and connects to another instance (stand-in for a self-hosted VM, `docs/SELF_HOSTING.md`).
the first load of a launcher-served UI seeds one backend `Local` (id `default-local`) with the page origin and the injected key.

`--host 0.0.0.0` warns, listens on the machine's LAN address, and serves an index.html that carries `__AGENT_CANVAS_AUTH_REQUIRED__` and neither `__AGENT_CANVAS_SESSION_API_KEY__` nor the key itself (the loopback launcher's page carries the key marker); the UI behaves like `--public` (Add a backend with Next disabled; Skip leads to the API-key screen).

the opt-in the launcher's warning recommends (`--allow-lan-session-key`) should restore key injection on a LAN bind. Known failure (reproduced 2026-10-08): the npm launcher ignores the flag and the page still carries only `__AGENT_CANVAS_AUTH_REQUIRED__`; [#17949](https://github.com/OpenHands/OpenHands/issues/17949).
`OH_BIND_HOST=0.0.0.0` (the environment form of `--host`) prints the same two "not loopback" warnings and does not inject the session key, even with `LOCAL_BACKEND_API_KEY` set.

when the requested automation backend exits before it is ready, the launcher should print no success banner, stop the services it started and exit nonzero with the automation's exit reason. Known failure (reproduced 2026-10-13, #18362): it prints the **Main UI** banner and keeps the stack up with `/api/automation/health` answering `502`.

every launcher-served web stack hosts the DigitalOcean Managed Agents bridge on its ingress by default (`MARS_WEB=0` opts out): `/mars/health` answers `{"ok":true,"authRequired":true}` on a full, `--backend-only`, `--frontend-only` and `--host 0.0.0.0` launcher, `/mars/rpc/*` answers `401` without the session key and works with it, the static child behind the ingress hosts none, and the Electron stack hosts none either (its preload provides `window.marsBridge`).

`/server_info.runtime_services` lists the agent-server, ingress, frontend and automation URLs as the agent sees them, and a new conversation's system prompt carries a matching `<RUNTIME_SERVICES>` block.

with that block alone, the agent can reach the automation backend from its terminal: asked to, it reads the OpenAPI at the URL the block names, creates an enabled cron automation, and dispatches a run that completes; the automation and its run show up in the Automations UI.

`npm run build:lib` produces `dist/` where every `package.json` `exports` target exists and the main entry exports `AgentServerUIProviders`, `AgentServerUIRoot`, `CloudOrganizationBoundary` and the telemetry helpers.
all bundled CSS is scoped under `[data-agent-server-ui]`, and theme tokens such as `--oh-color-base` live on that scope root (observable in the standalone app).
mounted in a separate host app, Canvas styles stay inside the scope and `styleOverrides` restyle it. Blocked: no host-app example exists.

`docker run ghcr.io/openhands/agent-canvas` serves Canvas at `/canvas`; without `AGENT_CANVAS_ALLOW_LAN_SESSION_KEY=true` the UI asks for the key. Blocked without a Docker daemon. On a host whose kernel has no IPv6 (no `/proc/net/if_inet6`) the entrypoint logs `IPv6 is not available; binding the frontend to 0.0.0.0.` and the container keeps running (#18180).
`OH_CONVERSATION_RUNTIME=docker` runs each new conversation in its own container. Blocked without a Docker daemon.
`helm install agent-canvas ./helm/agent-canvas` runs the Docker image as a Kubernetes StatefulSet with a PVC and an Ingress. Blocked without `helm` and a cluster.
the Electron app first shows a dark splash (logo, **OpenHands Agent Canvas**, spinner, `Starting backend services…`, then live service-log lines, a first-launch note and **Show details**).
after boot a native window with a File/Edit/View/Window menu loads `http://localhost:8000` with the key injected (first run, no API-key screen).

on macOS the desktop window hides the native title bar and reserves a 28 px drag band (`titlebar-drag-region`, `aria-hidden`) above the shell, so the sidebar logo clears the traffic lights and the window can be dragged; the band is dropped in native fullscreen, also after a reload while fullscreen. Linux and Windows windows and browser tabs render no band (`window.desktopShell` is undefined in a tab; `platform` is `linux` on Linux). The band is rendered by the root layout, its error shell and the config-loading spinner, not by the first-run onboarding screen. Blocked without macOS (#17474).
external links in the desktop window open in the system browser for allowed schemes only. Not driven: the harness cannot click inside the Electron window.

scenarios.name: F26--version
scenarios.title: Version
scenarios.body: Run `node bin/agent-canvas.mjs --version; echo "exit=$?"` and `node bin/agent-canvas.mjs -v; echo "exit=$?"`. Each prints one line equal to `jq -r .version package.json` (the checkout's package version, which changes with every release: compare, do not expect a number; e.g. `[ "$(node bin/agent-canvas.mjs --version)" = "$(jq -r .version package.json)" ] && echo same`) and `exit=0`.
scenarios.raw: **Version (`F26.cli-version`).** Run `node bin/agent-canvas.mjs --version; echo "exit=$?"` and `node bin/agent-canvas.mjs -v; echo "exit=$?"`. Each prints one line equal to `jq -r .version package.json` (the checkout's package version, which changes with every release: compare, do not expect a number; e.g. `[ "$(node bin/agent-canvas.mjs --version)" = "$(jq -r .version package.json)" ] && echo same`) and `exit=0`.
expected: `--version` and `-v` print the package version and exit 0.

scenarios.name: F26--info
scenarios.title: Info
scenarios.body: Run `node bin/agent-canvas.mjs --info`. It prints `@openhands/agent-canvas <version>` (the `--version` value), `Default stack versions:` with `agent-server: <pin>` and `automation: <pin>`, `Compatibility:` `agent-server: >= <minimum>`, `Default ports:` `ingress: 8000`, `agent-server: 18000`, `automation: 18001`, and the override variables `OH_AGENT_SERVER_VERSION, OH_AGENT_SERVER_GIT_REF, OH_AGENT_SERVER_LOCAL_PATH` / `OH_AUTOMATION_VERSION, OH_AUTOMATION_GIT_REF`. The three versions are read from `config/defaults.json` (`versions.agentServer`, `versions.automation`, `compatibility.minimumAgentServer`) and move with every pin bump, so compare them with the file instead of expecting numbers: `test "$(node bin/agent-canvas.mjs --info | awk '/^(Default stack versions|Compatibility):/{s=1;next} /^$/{s=0} s{print $NF}' | paste -sd' ' -)" = "$(jq -r '[.versions.agentServer,.versions.automation,.compatibility.minimumAgentServer]|join(" ")' config/defaults.json)" && echo match || echo mismatch` prints `match`, and `printf '%s\n' "$(jq -r .compatibility.minimumAgentServer config/defaults.json)" "$(jq -r .versions.agentServer config/defaults.json)" | sort -VC && echo pin-meets-minimum || echo below-minimum` prints `pin-meets-minimum` (the default Agent Server passes the UI's own version gate).
scenarios.raw: **Info (`F26.cli-info`).** Run `node bin/agent-canvas.mjs --info`. It prints `@openhands/agent-canvas <version>` (the `--version` value), `Default stack versions:` with `agent-server: <pin>` and `automation: <pin>`, `Compatibility:` `agent-server: >= <minimum>`, `Default ports:` `ingress: 8000`, `agent-server: 18000`, `automation: 18001`, and the override variables `OH_AGENT_SERVER_VERSION, OH_AGENT_SERVER_GIT_REF, OH_AGENT_SERVER_LOCAL_PATH` / `OH_AUTOMATION_VERSION, OH_AUTOMATION_GIT_REF`. expected: `--info` prints the package version, the default agent-server and automation pins, the minimum agent-server version, the default ports and the override env vars.

scenarios.name: F26--public-mode-needs-a-key
scenarios.title: Public mode needs a key
scenarios.body: Run `T=$(mktemp -d); env -u LOCAL_BACKEND_API_KEY HOME=$T OH_CANVAS_SAFE_STATE_DIR=$T/state timeout 60 node bin/agent-canvas.mjs --public --port 18990; echo "exit=$?"; rm -rf $T`. After `✓ uvx found` it prints `✗ PUBLIC MODE requires LOCAL_BACKEND_API_KEY environment variable.` and `exit=1`. (The successful `--public` launch is `control-openhands launch --new --public`, mapped in F01.)

After `✓ uvx found` it prints `✗ PUBLIC MODE requires LOCAL_BACKEND_API_KEY environment variable.` and `exit=1`. (The successful `--public` launch is `control-openhands launch --new --public`, mapped in F01.)
expected: `--public` without `LOCAL_BACKEND_API_KEY` exits 1 with guidance.
notes: Known issue [OpenHands/software-agent-sdk#5731](https://github.com/OpenHands/software-agent-sdk/issues/5731) (`F26.cli-public-needs-key`): whitespace-only session keys remain configured credentials in the Agent Server. The Canvas launcher forwards a nonempty `LOCAL_BACKEND_API_KEY` verbatim, so a whitespace-only deployment value can leave the public login unable to use its intended key. Recheck an owned loopback-only public deployment with a whitespace-only supplied key, its actual HTTP/WebSocket authentication and a normal nonblank control; never test the server's default broad bind on an exposed interface. The SDK's missing-`OH_SECRET_KEY` cipher fallback is a separate configuration branch from a Canvas launcher that supplies an encryption key.

scenarios.name: F26--loopback-only-ingress
scenarios.title: Loopback-only ingress
scenarios.body:
Your run was started without `--host`. Run `P=$(control-openhands status | jq -r .ports.ingress); curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' http://127.0.0.1:$P/` (`200`), then find the machine's own address portably, `LAN=$(node -e 'for (const a of Object.values(require("os").networkInterfaces()).flat()) if (a.family === "IPv4" && !a.internal) { console.log(a.address); break }'); echo "LAN=$LAN"`, and `curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' --connect-timeout 3 http://$LAN:$P/; echo "exit=$?"`. At that address curl prints `000` and `exit=7` (connection refused). If `LAN` is empty the machine has no non-loopback address: record the loopback half and leave the refused-connection half `not-run` with that reason (it is the behavior this ID asserts, so an empty `LAN` is never a pass). Read-only second view, Linux form: `awk -v p=$(printf '%04X' $P) 'NR>1 && $4=="0A" && $2 ~ ":"p"$" {print $2}' /proc/net/tcp` prints only `0100007F:` (`127.0.0.1` in `/proc/net/tcp`'s byte order; elsewhere list the listener with the OS's socket tool, for example `ss -ltn 'sport = :'$P` or `lsof -nP -iTCP:$P -sTCP:LISTEN`, and expect `127.0.0.1:

` only), and `grep -a 'Listening on' $OH_VERIFY_RUN/private/stack.log` shows the ingress banner `Listening on: http://localhost:

/`. The LAN half of `F26.host-bind-lan` below is the contrast: there the same curl answers `200`.

At that address curl prints `000` and `exit=7` (connection refused). If `LAN` is empty the machine has no non-loopback address: record the loopback half and leave the refused-connection half `not-run` with that reason (it is the behavior this ID asserts, so an empty `LAN` is never a pass). Read-only second view, Linux form: `awk -v p=$(printf '%04X' $P) 'NR>1 && $4=="0A" && $2 ~ ":"p"$" {print $2}' /proc/net/tcp` prints only `0100007F:` (`127.0.0.1` in `/proc/net/tcp`'s byte order; elsewhere list the listener with the OS's socket tool, for example `ss -ltn 'sport = :'$P` or `lsof -nP -iTCP:$P -sTCP:LISTEN`, and expect `127.0.0.1:

` only), and `grep -a 'Listening on' $OH_VERIFY_RUN/private/stack.log` shows the ingress banner `Listening on: http://localhost:

expected: from a normal Canvas, backend selector → **Add Backend** → **Agent-server** → **Remote** shows the self-hosting guidance and connects to another instance (stand-in for a self-hosted VM, `docs/SELF_HOSTING.md`).
notes: Known issue [#15434](https://github.com/OpenHands/OpenHands/issues/15434) (`F26.remote-backend`): The embedded VS Code action on a self-hosted reverse-proxy origin was reported to reopen Canvas because its advertised URL omitted the separate editor port/path. Current launchers include an ingress `/vscode/` route; recheck against the affected HTTPS proxy deployment with an actually available editor binary and emitted URL before concluding resolution. This run lacks that self-hosted proxy/editor deployment.

Known issue [OpenHands/software-agent-sdk#5373](https://github.com/OpenHands/software-agent-sdk/issues/5373) (`F26.remote-backend`): A self-hosted Agent Server using default Rich traceback logging can wedge its event loop and grow memory when a websocket error has a cyclic/deep exception chain; Canvas then times out or disconnects. The npm launcher forces JSON logging, so rechecking needs a separately hosted default-Rich backend plus the reported pathological peer/backlog reproducer and bounded memory/time isolation. That original peer/driver is not included in the issue body; do not synthesize a server patch or stress the shared host and claim a live UI reproduction.

scenarios.name: F26--managed-agents-bridge
scenarios.title: Managed Agents bridge
scenarios.body: With both partial stacks up: `curl -s "$(control-openhands status | jq -r .baseUrl)/mars/health"`, `curl -s http://127.0.0.1:18960/mars/health` and `curl -s http://127.0.0.1:18970/mars/health` each print `{"ok":true,"authRequired":true}`, while `curl -s "http://127.0.0.1:$(control-openhands status | jq -r .ports.frontend)/mars/health" | head -c 15` prints `<!DOCTYPE html>` (the static child behind your run's ingress has no second bridge). `curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' -X POST http://127.0.0.1:18960/mars/rpc/getAuthState` is `401` (no key). The frontend-only page has the bridge but no key to use it: after the cross-connect, `control-openhands browser eval "({marsBridge: !!window.marsBridge, key: Boolean(window.__AGENT_CANVAS_SESSION_API_KEY__)})"` on `http://127.0.0.1:18970/` is `{marsBridge: true, key: false}` (what that does to DigitalOcean sign-in is F25's `F25.digitalocean-sign-in` known failure).

scenarios.name: F26--lan-bind
scenarios.title: LAN bind
scenarios.body: Start a full stack on all interfaces: `Q=$OH_VERIFY_RUN/private/f26-lan; mkdir -p $Q; HOME=$Q/home OH_CANVAS_SAFE_STATE_DIR=$Q/state OH_CANVAS_SAFE_BACKEND_PORT=18961 OH_CANVAS_SAFE_AUTOMATION_PORT=18962 OH_CANVAS_SAFE_VITE_PORT=18963 LOCAL_BACKEND_API_KEY=qa-f26-lan-key OH_SECRET_KEY=qa-f26-secret DO_NOT_TRACK=1 nohup node bin/agent-canvas.mjs --host 0.0.0.0 --port 18960 > $Q/launcher.log 2>&1 & echo $! > $Q/pid`, and wait until `curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' http://127.0.0.1:18960/` is `200`. `grep -a 'not loopback' $Q/launcher.log` shows `[auth] Bind host 0.0.0.0 is not loopback — session key will not be injected into HTML` and `[static] WARNING: bind host 0.0.0.0 is not loopback; refusing to inject the session API key into HTML.` The served page proves it: `curl -s http://127.0.0.1:18960/ | grep -o '__AGENT_CANVAS_\(SESSION_API_KEY\|AUTH_REQUIRED\)__' | sort -u` prints only `__AGENT_CANVAS_AUTH_REQUIRED__` and `curl -s http://127.0.0.1:18960/ | grep -c qa-f26-lan-key` prints `0`, while your loopback run's page, `curl -s "$(control-openhands status | jq -r .baseUrl)/" | grep -o '__AGENT_CANVAS_\(SESSION_API_KEY\|AUTH_REQUIRED\)__' | sort -u`, prints only `__AGENT_CANVAS_SESSION_API_KEY__`. The bind is real: with `LAN` from the loopback bullet, `curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' --connect-timeout 3 http://$LAN:18960/` is `200` here (refused on your run, `F26.loopback-bind-default`; with an empty `LAN` this check is `not-run`). The browser part below expects a profile that has never visited `127.0.0.1:18960` (true in this file's order; on a repeat pass run `control-openhands browser reset` first and restore your run afterwards, see Gotchas). Then `control-openhands browser goto http://127.0.0.1:18960/ --allow-external` and `control-openhands browser eval "({key: Boolean(window.__AGENT_CANVAS_SESSION_API_KEY__), authRequired: window.__AGENT_CANVAS_AUTH_REQUIRED__ === true})"` → `{key: false, authRequired: true}`. Fill `testid=api-key-entry-name` with `QA_LAN` and `testid=api-key-entry-api-key` with `qa-f26-lan-key`, click `testid=api-key-entry-submit`; `control-openhands browser wait 'testid=root-layout' --timeout 10000` succeeds. A few seconds later the telemetry consent dialog for the new `QA_LAN` backend opens and blocks clicks; answer it (`role=button[name="Confirm preferences"]`) before driving that page further. Stop it with `kill -TERM $(cat $Q/pid)`.

scenarios.name: F26--generated-session-key-persists
scenarios.title: Generated session key persists
scenarios.body: With 18960–18963 free, define a helper and start a loopback stack without a key: `Q=$OH_VERIFY_RUN/private/f26-keys; mkdir -p $Q; start(){ HOME=$Q/home OH_CANVAS_SAFE_STATE_DIR=$Q/state OH_CANVAS_SAFE_BACKEND_PORT=18961 OH_CANVAS_SAFE_AUTOMATION_PORT=18962 OH_CANVAS_SAFE_VITE_PORT=18963 OH_SECRET_KEY=qa-f26-secret DO_NOT_TRACK=1 "$@" > $Q/launcher.log 2>&1 & echo $! > $Q/pid; for i in $(seq 1 60); do c=$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' http://127.0.0.1:18960/); [ "$c" = 200 ] && break; sleep 3; done; echo "code=$c"; }; start env -u LOCAL_BACKEND_API_KEY nohup node bin/agent-canvas.mjs --port 18960` (`code=200`). `curl -s http://127.0.0.1:18960/ | grep -o '__AGENT_CANVAS_SESSION_API_KEY__[^;<]*' | md5sum` prints a hash (never print the key itself); `$Q/home/.openhands/agent-canvas/api-key.txt` exists (64 hex characters) and `curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' -H "X-Session-API-Key: $(cat $Q/home/.openhands/agent-canvas/api-key.txt)" http://127.0.0.1:18960/api/settings` is `200`. `kill -TERM $(cat $Q/pid); sleep 6`, run the same `start ...` line again in the same shell and repeat the `md5sum` line: the hash is identical.

scenarios.name: F26--runtime-services
scenarios.title: Runtime services
scenarios.body: Run `control-openhands api GET /server_info --pick runtime_services.mode` (`agent-canvas`) and `control-openhands api GET /server_info --pick runtime_services.services.automation.url_from_agent` (`http://localhost:<automation port>`; `control-openhands status` prints the ports). Then `control-openhands conversation start --prompt "Reply with the single word: ok" --wait --timeout 180` (prints `<id>`) and `control-openhands conversation events <id> --grep RUNTIME_SERVICES --from-start`: the `SystemPromptEvent` matches, with an excerpt `<RUNTIME_SERVICES>\nYou are running inside an agent-canvas dev stack started ...`. `control-openhands conversation events <id> --grep "localhost:<automation port>" --from-start` shows `* Automation backend: http://localhost:<port>` plus its `Docs:` and `OpenAPI:` URLs.
scenarios.raw: **Runtime services (`F26.runtime-services`).** Run `control-openhands api GET /server_info --pick runtime_services.mode` (`agent-canvas`) and `control-openhands api GET /server_info --pick runtime_services.services.automation.url_from_agent` (`http://localhost:<automation port>`; `control-openhands status` prints the ports). Then `control-openhands conversation start --prompt "Reply with the single word: ok" --wait --timeout 180` (prints `<id>`) and `control-openhands conversation events <id> --grep RUNTIME_SERVICES --from-start`: the `SystemPromptEvent` matches, with an excerpt `<RUNTIME_SERVICES>\nYou are running inside an agent-canvas dev stack started ...`. `control-openhands conversation events <id> --grep "localhost:<automation port>" --from-start` shows `* Automation backend: http://localhost:<port>` plus its `Docs:` and `OpenAPI:` URLs.
expected: `/server_info.runtime_services` lists the agent-server, ingress, frontend and automation URLs as the agent sees them, and a new conversation's system prompt carries a matching `<RUNTIME_SERVICES>` block.
notes: Known issue [#16720](https://github.com/OpenHands/OpenHands/issues/16720) (`F26.runtime-services`): CPU-heavy commands in several conversations can starve Agent Server and stop the UI loading; the report requests lower priority for agent commands than the service. Recheck with a disposable bounded workload, recorded CPU/resource limits and real command observations, never arbitrary stress on the shared machine. The exact Rust workload and affected resource envelope are missing, and real agent execution needs a model key. The backend counterpart is [OpenHands/software-agent-sdk#4575](https://github.com/OpenHands/software-agent-sdk/issues/4575).

Known issue [#16690](https://github.com/OpenHands/OpenHands/issues/16690) (`F26.docker-image` `F26.runtime-services`): A Docker deployment with nine chats becomes slow/disconnected, then reloads lose the list and startup proxies report ECONNREFUSED. Recheck on the affected Windows-host Docker configuration with retained conversation state and a controlled workload; creating a few empty local chats cannot prove the reported resource/runtime failure. This run lacks Docker and the original conversation/workload fixture.

Known issue [#16300](https://github.com/OpenHands/OpenHands/issues/16300) (`F26.runtime-services`): The npm launcher can fail while building LiteLLM native dependencies when resolved AWS crates require a newer Rust compiler, leaving backend services unavailable. Recheck an isolated uncached uv environment with `litellm==1.95.0`, the reported Rust 1.93.1/toolchain/platform and dependency resolution; a warm current backend cache cannot exercise that install failure. The historical dependency/toolchain fixture is unavailable.

Known issue [#16208](https://github.com/OpenHands/OpenHands/issues/16208) (`F26.runtime-services`): On Fedora Rawhide/Python 3.14.6, settings work but starting any conversation returns HTTP 500. Recheck a native Fedora environment with the reported SDK/runtime and model/profile, including the underlying server traceback; this macOS current-runtime stack cannot prove that platform-specific failure.

Known issue [OpenHands/software-agent-sdk#4901](https://github.com/OpenHands/software-agent-sdk/issues/4901) (`F26.runtime-services`): closing an ACP conversation on POSIX is reported to leave the adapter's descendant Node/CLI processes alive after the top npm process exits. Recheck an owned authenticated ACP provider command chain, record its exact descendant identities before close and inspect only those identities afterwards; cleanup must target those owned groups. The current run has no authorized authenticated ACP runtime for this path.

Known issue [OpenHands/software-agent-sdk#5974](https://github.com/OpenHands/software-agent-sdk/issues/5974) (`F26.runtime-services`; workspace picker in F03): a saved-workspace mutation waiting for its registry file lock can block the Agent Server event loop, including `/alive`, until the lock is released. Recheck only an owned registry using a bounded lock holder, an independently confirmed waiting mutation, concurrent liveness probes and a successful post-release readback; the original evidence uses Linux kernel lock-wait readback. A healthy idle server or concurrent writes without deliberate lock contention do not cover it.

scenarios.name: F26--blocked
scenarios.title: Blocked
scenarios.body: If `docker info` cannot reach the daemon but `dockerd` is installed, start it (`setsid dockerd`); without one, record both Docker rows `blocked` naming the missing daemon. With a daemon, run the image with `-p 127.0.0.1:8000:8000`, open `http://localhost:8000/canvas` and expect the **Add a backend** step (`testid=onboarding-step-check-backend`, Next disabled until a key is typed); `onboarding-skip` leads to `testid=api-key-entry-screen`. With `-e AGENT_CANVAS_ALLOW_LAN_SESSION_KEY=true` the key is injected and first run opens on Choose your agent, under the telemetry consent dialog. `npm run build:docker` behind a TLS-intercepting proxy needs the proxy CA inside the build stages (without it `uv pip install` / `pip install` in the final stage fail with `CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED: self-signed certificate in certificate chain`), and Docker Hub may answer 429. Build a scratch copy of the Dockerfile that only adds the CA, never an edited `docker/Dockerfile`: after `FROM node:24-slim AS frontend-build` add `COPY --from=ccrca ca-bundle.crt /tmp/qa-ca.crt` and `ENV NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS=/tmp/qa-ca.crt npm_config_cafile=/tmp/qa-ca.crt`, after the first `USER root` add the same `COPY` and `ENV SSL_CERT_FILE=/tmp/qa-ca.crt PIP_CERT=/tmp/qa-ca.crt REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE=/tmp/qa-ca.crt UV_NATIVE_TLS=1`, then `docker build -f <copy> --build-context ccrca=<dir holding ca-bundle.crt> --network host --build-arg AGENT_SERVER_IMAGE=<images.agentServer>:<versions.agentServer>-python --build-arg AGENT_SERVER_VERSION=<versions.agentServer> --build-arg AUTOMATION_VERSION=<versions.automation> --build-arg VITE_BASE_PATH=/canvas -t qa-agent-canvas:target .` (the pins `scripts/docker-build.mjs` reads from `config/defaults.json`; about 5 min on a warm cache). Publish it on a free port (`-p 127.0.0.1:<free>:8000`; 8000 and the 188xx blocks may belong to other runs). Docker Hub may answer `429 Too Many Requests` for `node:24-slim`; in the scratch copy only, replace both `FROM node:24-slim` lines with `FROM mirror.gcr.io/library/node:24-slim` (arrange; say so in the note). Run the unmodified image with `docker run -d --name <qa-name> -p 127.0.0.1:<free>:8000 qa-agent-canvas:target`. On a kernel without IPv6, `docker logs <qa-name>` shows `IPv6 is not available; binding the frontend to 0.0.0.0.` and `Static-server + proxy listening on http://0.0.0.0:8000/canvas/`, `/canvas/` answers `200` within about 25 s and `docker inspect -f '{{.State.Status}}' <qa-name>` is still `running` minutes later (#18178 fixed by #18180, verified 2026-10-13); `docker exec <qa-name> ls /opt/agent-canvas` lists the `mars-*.mjs` bridge modules (#18343). The container's generated key is `docker exec <qa-name> cat /home/openhands/.openhands/agent-canvas/api-key.txt` (write it to `$OH_VERIFY_RUN/private/`, fill with `--value-file`). Settings → Application (`/canvas/settings/app`) shows the image's `Version` (`agent-canvas-update-card`), which matches `jq -r .version package.json`. Remove the containers and the image afterwards (`docker rm -f`, `docker rmi`). Record `F26.lib-host-app` `blocked` naming the missing host-app example. `command -v helm kubectl` prints nothing here: record `F26.helm-chart` `blocked` naming the missing `helm` binary and cluster; with them, `helm lint helm/agent-canvas` and `helm template qa helm/agent-canvas` render the StatefulSet, Service and Ingress, and `helm install` follows `helm/agent-canvas/README.md`.

This run lacks Docker and the original conversation/workload fixture.

Blocked without Docker.

scenarios.name: F26--desktop-splash-and-window
scenarios.title: Desktop splash and window
scenarios.body: Start a private display and the app in one process group: `Q=$OH_VERIFY_RUN/private/f26-desktop; mkdir -p $Q/shots; setsid nohup sh -c "echo \$\$ > $Q/pgid; Xvfb :78 -screen 0 1440x1000x24 -nolisten tcp & sleep 1; DISPLAY=:78 HOME=$Q/home OH_CANVAS_SAFE_STATE_DIR=$Q/state LOCAL_BACKEND_API_KEY=qa-f26-desktop-key OH_SECRET_KEY=qa-f26-secret DO_NOT_TRACK=1 exec node_modules/.bin/electron --no-sandbox electron" > $Q/desktop.log 2>&1 &`, then capture frames: `for i in $(seq 1 40); do sleep 1; DISPLAY=:78 import -window root $Q/shots/s$(printf %02d $i).png; done`. Read the frames: the first seconds show the splash (logo, `OpenHands Agent Canvas`, `AI coding agent interface`, spinner, `Starting backend services…`, then lines such as `agent-server: {"asctime": ...`, the note `First launch downloads Python + the OpenHands agent server.` and a **Show details** button); a later frame shows the main window with a `File Edit View Window` menu and the first-run **Choose your agent** step under the consent dialog naming `the local backend "Local" at http://localhost:8000` (about 30 s on a warm cache, minutes on the first download). While it runs, `curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8000/mars/health | head -c 15` prints `<!DOCTYPE html>`: the desktop stack's ingress hosts no bridge (`marsWebBridge: false`, `F26.mars-web-bridge`). Copy the frames you cite into `$OH_VERIFY_RUN/evidence/F26.desktop-boot-splash/` and `.../F26.desktop-main-window/`. Stop in two steps: `kill -TERM $(cat $Q/pgid)` signals only the Electron launcher (it quits and stops its backend services); after about 10 s ports 8000, 18000, 18001 and 3001 are free again. Then `kill -TERM -- -$(cat $Q/pgid)` ends Xvfb; `ps -o pid,cmd -g $(cat $Q/pgid)` lists nothing.

scenarios.body: Temporarily replace only an owned Agent Server with its same pinned interpreter/state on the same port; unset `LOG_JSON`, `CI`, `GITHUB_ACTIONS` and `LOG_RICH_TRACEBACKS`, and retain its PID for cleanup. Create a bare-tool conversation whose dummy LLM points at closed `http://127.0.0.1:9/v1` with zero retries. Start 60 direct `/alive` probes concurrently with a genuine Canvas **Send message**; inspect the rendered connection error and final conversation status. families.title: Workspace tools: terminal, browser, planner, tasks and usage
families.overview:
The conversation's right-hand drawer holds the agent's workspace tools: a
read-only Terminal that mirrors the agent's shell commands, a Browser tab that
shows the agent browser tool's last screenshot, a Planner that renders
`.agents_tmp/PLAN.md` (or starts a planning helper), a Task List that mirrors
the agent's `task_tracker`, and a Usage tab with the context meter, a manual
"Compact context" action and token/cost totals. Around them sit the composer's
context-window ring, the chat header's Overview column (peek, pinnable rows,
secondary drawer), and two client tools the agent can call to drive the UI:
`canvas_ui_control` (open a tab or a file) and `launch_child_conversation`.
families.entry:
- Conversation header panel button (`right-panel-toggle`, aria "Show panel"), then a drawer tab: `conversation-tab-files`, `-commits`, `-tasklist` (only after the agent used `task_tracker`), `-planner`, `-terminal`, `-browser`, `-usage`. Clicking the active tab closes the drawer (F08).
- Drawer tabs menu: the "..." in `tabs-pane-header`, then `conversation-tabs-menu-open-<tab>` (also pin/unpin, F08).
- Direct URL `/conversations/<id>` (drawer closed after load) or `/conversations/<id>/panel` (full-width drawer with Back at 1024 px or narrower, the phone entry, F07.panel-route; wider, it redirects to `/conversations/<id>` with the drawer open).
- Composer context ring (`context-window-meter`) > Usage or bar; conversation "..." > Display Usage and Cost (F07.display-cost).
- Chat header (i) (`conversation-overview-toggle`): hover for the peek, click for the Overview column and its "..." menu.
- Composer `+` (`chat-plus-button`) > Show Available Skills / Hooks / Agent Tools & Metadata (also in the conversation "..." menu, F07).
- The agent itself: `canvas_ui_control` (open a tab or file), `launch_child_conversation`, and file-path links in its messages (`markdown-file-path-link`).
families.given:
Preconditions:

- Baseline state (launched, doctored, `onboard --skip` done) and `control-openhands llm preset deepseek` (every populated state needs real agent turns).
- Desktop viewport unless a bullet says phone.
- `F27.browser-screenshot` is blocked when the agent server logs `Error preloading chromium` (no browser tools in Agent Tools & Metadata > Available Tools); it needs an agent server with working Chromium.
- `F27.plugins-modal` needs a conversation started with at least one plugin (the menu item is hidden otherwise).
- `F27.terminal-waiting` needs a conversation in the error state: arrange one with a profile whose key is invalid (no model cost; see the bullet).
- `F27.usage-provider-balance` (card shown) needs an OpenRouter key; with DeepSeek only the hidden case is checkable.
- `F27.overview-identity` needs a repo with a GitHub origin, its own so the shared `qa-repo` of F08 keeps none: `control-openhands fixture git-repo --name qa-f27-repo --remote https://github.com/qa-example/qa-f27-repo.git` (`--remote` only sets `origin`, also when the repo already exists, which the output reports as `remoteChanged`; no model is needed for the rows).
families.gotchas:
- After a reload the Task List (and tab bar entry) appears only once history has loaded; wait about 2 s before counting `[data-active="true"]` rows.
- `[data-active]` is also used by sidebar conversation cards: always combine it with `has-text=<task title>`.
- `browser click --observe` takes a plain CSS selector (`'[data-testid=compact-context-button]'`); the `testid=` form fails with a `querySelectorAll` SyntaxError.
- "Create a plan" leaves that conversation in plan mode: the next composer message goes to the planner helper, which has no `launch_child_conversation` or `canvas_ui_control`. Use a separate conversation for client-tool prompts.
- The child-launch toast's Open link animates; `browser click` on it times out with "element is not stable". Read the child id from the parent's `[child-conversation]` message instead.
- `GET …/file/download?path=…/.agents_tmp/PLAN.md` 404 and `GET /api/llm/balance` 404 are expected app-origin errors (no plan yet; no balance endpoint). Count them in `browser errors --app-only` but do not report them.
- Escape closes the composer context popover and the Overview "..." menu and returns focus to the trigger (#18044); an outside click, or a second click on the trigger, closes them too.
- The Overview column is 28 px narrower than its content (`scrollWidth` 296, `clientWidth` 268). After some clicks inside it, Playwright's scroll-into-view shifts it and the card looks cut off on the left; `browser reload` restores it before taking screenshots.
- The agent may summarize a client-tool action with its own title (for example "Launch local child conversation to reply PONG") instead of "Launching a child conversation"; assert the toast and events, not the chat title.
- The Overview peek appears only while the drawer is open (`canPeekOnHover` needs `isRightPanelShown`); a `browser goto` or reload starts with the drawer closed.
- The Overview's repo and branch rows depend on a bash probe (`useLocalGitInfo`) that runs only while the conversation's status is idle, running, waiting for confirmation or finished and the agent is not in error. Right after `conversation start` the probe has run and its result stays cached on the page, but on an errored conversation a reload hides the rows again, and `conversation pause` does not apply to an errored conversation. Read the rows before any `goto` or `reload`.
- At phone width (and in a narrow drawer) the tab row shows only the tabs that fit; the rest are reachable only through the tabs menu (`conversation-tabs-menu-open-<tab>`), and which tabs fit depends on the active tab's label width.
- Plain `agent-canvas` instances on one machine share the tmux socket `/tmp/tmux-<uid>/openhands` ([OpenHands/OpenHands#17946](https://github.com/OpenHands/OpenHands/issues/17946)), so another instance stopping can reset this one's terminal. `control-openhands launch` gives each run its own `TMUX_TMPDIR`, so in verification runs a reset means this run's agent server restarted.
- Agent Tools & Metadata remembers the last tab (it reopens on Available Tools).
- The Overview menu opens only Pull Requests (`conversation-overview-menu-open-git-pull_requests`); its testids are `conversation-overview-menu-open-*` and `-pin-*` for `workspace` and the Git rows only.
- Known open issues: terminal history after reload ([#17566](https://github.com/OpenHands/OpenHands/issues/17566)) still fails (reproduced 2026-10-06); info modals at phone width (#17562) pass.
- Agent tab requests (`open_tab`, `navigate_to_file`, chat file links) are saved per conversation like a user tab click (#18045): after the agent opens Terminal or a file and the page reloads, the drawer starts closed and the panel toggle reopens it on that tab; clicking that tab then closes the drawer. At phone width they navigate to `/conversations/<id>/panel`.
- Known issue [#17774](https://github.com/OpenHands/OpenHands/issues/17774) (`F27.planner-empty` `F27.planner-plan`): Planner reads on a native Windows local backend reject drive-letter/mixed-separator workspace paths with `Conversation file path must stay inside the workspace` before a download request. Recheck both a scratch workspace and an opened drive-letter workspace, with and without `.agents_tmp/PLAN.md`; this run lacks a Windows local Agent Server.
- Known issue [#17198](https://github.com/OpenHands/OpenHands/issues/17198) (`F27.terminal-output`): Native Windows desktop agents intermittently return `[Command finished execution with no output]` for real file-listing/terminal commands and retry them. Recheck with the affected Windows installer/runtime, project agent definitions and an exact command/workspace; no deterministic pattern or backend trace is provided, and this run has no Windows desktop runtime. The backend counterpart is [OpenHands/software-agent-sdk#4963](https://github.com/OpenHands/software-agent-sdk/issues/4963).
- Known issue [#16551](https://github.com/OpenHands/OpenHands/issues/16551) (`F27.browser-screenshot`): On native Windows, the browser tool chooses system Chrome over installed Playwright Chromium and times out before returning state/screenshots. Recheck default browser selection and an explicit executable-path control on a Windows host with both browsers and the reported browser_use runtime; the verification Chromium itself is a different tool. Blocked here without Windows and real browser-tool execution credentials.
- Known issue [#16581](https://github.com/OpenHands/OpenHands/issues/16581) (`F27.terminal-output`): A module-scoped terminal command index can suppress output in a second simultaneously mounted Terminal and reset the first when either unmounts. The report describes a future split-panel/embedded concurrent mount rather than a supported standalone entry point. Recheck in a host that actually mounts two independent Canvas Terminal consumers with real command histories; the current harness has one Terminal route and no such host fixture.
- Known issue [#17384](https://github.com/OpenHands/OpenHands/issues/17384) (`F27.launch-child`): A file-based delegated subagent using a saved profile/provider connection can fail with HTTP 401 while the top-level conversation succeeds, because encrypted provider credentials are not decrypted in that backend factory path. Recheck a reviewed `.agents/agents/` worker, encrypted provider connection and saved profile using a real key, comparing parent and worker authentication. This is a delegated SDK subagent path, distinct from the client-tool child-launch recipe; neither a dummy key nor an unencrypted profile proves it.
- Known issue [OpenHands/software-agent-sdk#5533](https://github.com/OpenHands/software-agent-sdk/issues/5533) (`F27.terminal-output`): A slow interactive Bash startup can make the first terminal command return early with empty output and a false successful exit code. Recheck both standalone and pooled tmux using a private `.bashrc` with `sleep 0.4`, then a bounded `sleep 2` first command and its real observation. The shell fixture can be arranged, but the mapped agent-command/Terminal path cannot run here without a model key.
- Known issue [OpenHands/software-agent-sdk#5322](https://github.com/OpenHands/software-agent-sdk/issues/5322) (`F27.terminal-output`): The default tmux pane pool or Windows terminal can let `git log -p` start an interactive pager, so the next agent command receives stale paged output instead of its own result. Recheck a reviewed large git fixture, a real installed pager and a follow-up marker command on each affected terminal backend. The fixture is arrangeable, but the mapped agent-tool path needs a model key (and the Windows half needs Windows).
- Known issue [#17383](https://github.com/OpenHands/OpenHands/issues/17383) (`F27.browser-screenshot`; dependency counterpart [OpenHands/software-agent-sdk#5152](https://github.com/OpenHands/software-agent-sdk/issues/5152)): unlocked dependency resolution can silently remove the agent's browser tools. The actual 2026-10-12 pinned runtime resolves browser-use 0.11.13, mcp 1.30.0 and fastmcp 3.4.8; its genuine BrowserToolExecutor constructs successfully. That narrowly fails to reproduce the SDK report's specified mcp 2.x import failure. Fresh constructor recheck on 2026-10-16 at `b34ac59`, using the actual Agent Server 1.55.0 interpreter and private HOME, again resolves browser-use 0.11.13, mcp 1.30.0 and fastmcp 3.4.8 and constructs successfully; no browser operation or model was run. The Canvas/global browser-operation path still needs an authorized real LLM and a genuine browser-enabled agent issuing a `browser_*` operation; construction alone does not establish that feature works.
- Browser availability also depends on [OpenHands/software-agent-sdk#5899](https://github.com/OpenHands/software-agent-sdk/issues/5899) (`F27.browser-screenshot`; canonical tool-selection note in F13): a Chromium installed only under `PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH` is missed by the agent-tool probe. Recheck the real browser-tool operation on a host with only that custom cache and no standard browser, default cache or PATH executable. This Mac's user Chrome must remain installed; an executor constructor or the verification browser is not a successful agent browser operation.
- Known issue [OpenHands/software-agent-sdk#5835](https://github.com/OpenHands/software-agent-sdk/issues/5835) (`F27.overview-identity`): the local Overview Git probe uses conversation-scoped Bash execution; an idle-eviction pass can kill scoped work without a final output. Recheck a disposable short-idle-TTL server while a genuine Canvas Git probe is still executing, with independently observed command lifetime and the eventual output/result. The report's standalone asynchronous `sleep` reproduction is supporting backend evidence, not proof of a Terminal-tab command, which uses the agent event stream instead.

features.description: with the runtime active and no command run yet, the Terminal tab reads "No terminal output yet. Commands run by the agent will appear here."

while the runtime is starting or the conversation is in an error state, the Terminal tab reads "Waiting for runtime to start..."; a paused (stopped) conversation shows the empty message instead, by design.
the agent's commands appear as `$ <command>` followed by their output; typing into the terminal does nothing (stdin is disabled).
after a page reload the earlier commands and output are still shown (issue [#17566](https://github.com/OpenHands/OpenHands/issues/17566)).
a command the agent runs while the page is open is appended live.

before any browsing the URL bar reads "No URL loaded", "Open in New Tab" is a disabled button, and the body reads "No page loaded yet. Ask OpenHands to open a URL. Example: "Open https://example.com"".
after the agent's browser tool ran, the tab shows the last screenshot under a bar with its URL and an enabled "Open in New Tab" link.
with no plan the Planner reads "There is currently no plan for this repo" with an enabled "Create a plan" button; the drawer's "Build ⌘↩" button is disabled.
"Create a plan" toasts "Planning agent initialized", switches the composer to plan mode ("Let’s work on a plan") and disables itself, also after a reload.
when the workspace has `.agents_tmp/PLAN.md`, the Planner renders it as Markdown with an enabled "Build ⌘↩" bar.
"Build ⌘↩" sends "Execute the plan based on the .agents_tmp/PLAN.md file." to the agent.
the Task List tab appears only once the agent used `task_tracker`; it lists each task with its status icon and highlights the in-progress one; the drawer's tabs menu opens it too.

the Usage tab shows the context meter ("X% used (Y% left)", tokens / window), Token Usage (Input, Cache Hit, Cache Write, Output, Total) and Total Cost. Above 70% fill, the meter label and bar use the warning feedback role; above 90%, its label uses error feedback and its bar uses status error. Text reaches 4.5:1 against the raised Usage surface and fills reach 3:1 against the track in all five themes.
before any metrics arrive the Usage tab reads "No metrics data available".

"Compact context" (agent idle) toasts "Context compaction started" then "Context compacted" (or "…freed N tokens"), and the agent server records a Condensation; the (i) tooltip explains it. Above 70% fill, "Context filling up" uses the theme warning feedback color.
the provider balance card shows only when the agent server reports a balance (OpenRouter); otherwise it is absent without an error message.

the composer's context ring opens a popover with the fill label, a Compact context button, tokens and a Usage item; the bar or Usage item opens the Usage tab; Escape (focus returns to the ring) or an outside click closes it.
while the drawer is open, hovering the chat header (i) button shows a peek of the Overview rows (with the drawer closed there is no peek; clicking opens the column).
the Overview "..." menu pins and unpins rows (Workspace, Git parts); an unpinned row stays hidden after a reload.
the Overview Changes row closes the Overview and opens the drawer on Commits.
the Overview "..." menu's Git > Commits item opens the drawer on Commits with Uncommitted collapsed; Git > Changes opens Commits with Uncommitted expanded; both close the Overview.

the Overview's Workspace row shows the attached folder's basename (`None` without a workspace), and once the workspace's `origin` is a GitHub remote the Git block adds an `owner/repo` link to the repository and a branch link.
Overview menu > Pull Requests opens the secondary drawer with a close button; without a git repository it reads "Connect a git repository to view pull requests and issues".
the agent's `canvas_ui_control` `open_tab` opens the drawer on the requested tab (files, browser, terminal, planner, tasklist), and the choice persists like a user tab click.
`canvas_ui_control` `navigate_to_file` (and clicking a file path in chat) opens Files with that file selected.
at phone width an agent `open_tab` makes the requested tab visible on `/conversations/<id>/panel`.

the agent's `launch_child_conversation` (local) toasts "Launched a local child conversation" with an Open link; the child runs, and the launch result (`[child-conversation] {"status":"launched",…}` with the child id) is posted back to the parent agent as a user message.
the composer `+` menu's Skills, Hooks and Agent Tools & Metadata modals fit a 390 px viewport (issue #17562); content is covered by F07.
a conversation started with plugins offers a plugins item that lists `active-plugin-<name>` rows.
at 390 px the panel route shows the Usage, Task List and Planner tabs without overflow, and the tab row stays visible.

Do not run any tools.' Then reply OK."` and poll `control-openhands browser toasts` every few seconds: one toast reads `Launched a local child conversation Open`. Take the child id from `control-openhands conversation events <tools-id> --kinds MessageEvent` (the `[child-conversation] {"status":"launched",…,"conversation_id":"<child-id>"…}` message), then `control-openhands conversation wait <child-id> --timeout 120` (`finished`) and `control-openhands conversation events <child-id> --kinds MessageEvent` (agent `PONG`). `control-openhands browser count 'testid=conversation-card >> has-text=PONG'` is `1`.

This is a delegated SDK subagent path, distinct from the client-tool child-launch recipe; neither a dummy key nor an unencrypted profile proves it.

Known issue [#17383](https://github.com/OpenHands/OpenHands/issues/17383) (`F27.browser-screenshot`; dependency counterpart [OpenHands/software-agent-sdk#5152](https://github.com/OpenHands/software-agent-sdk/issues/5152)): unlocked dependency resolution can silently remove the agent's browser tools. The actual 2026-10-12 pinned runtime resolves browser-use 0.11.13, mcp 1.30.0 and fastmcp 3.4.8; its genuine BrowserToolExecutor constructs successfully. That narrowly fails to reproduce the SDK report's specified mcp 2.x import failure. Fresh constructor recheck on 2026-10-16 at `b34ac59`, using the actual Agent Server 1.55.0 interpreter and private HOME, again resolves browser-use 0.11.13, mcp 1.30.0 and fastmcp 3.4.8 and constructs successfully; no browser operation or model was run. families.title: Automation setup page
families.overview:
The setup page is the one form for making and changing automations outside the
template dialog. **Add Automation → Create Automation** opens it blank at
`/automations/setup`; a saved draft reopens at `/automations/setup?draftId=<id>`;
kebab **Edit** opens an existing automation at
`/automations/setup?automationId=<id>`. The form collects Name, a Prompt (or
Custom Python with entrypoint and setup script), agent profile, model and
repositories, a Schedule or Event trigger, and optional plugins and timeout.
A docked composer under the form can ask the agent to fill it. Create mode's
toolbar has **Save draft**, **Test** and **Create Automation**; edit mode's has
**Test**, **Save** and **Close**. A server-backed draft carries the server's
validation result and test runs; Create turns it into a real, enabled
automation and removes the draft.

F22 keeps `F22.agent-assisted-setup` (the end-to-end agent, plugin, phone and
draft-Test recipes); F23 owns edit mode (`F23.edit-*`, including Test and the save state on the edit
page). This family gives each create-mode behavior its own ID so a pass can fail one without
failing the others.
families.entry:
- Dashboard header **Add Automation → Create Automation** (`automations-add-automation`, then `automations-add-automation-create`): blank create mode. Every create recipe below starts here.
- Empty dashboard **Create Automation** (`automations-empty >> automations-create-automation`): the same blank form (`F21.empty-state`).
- Dashboard Drafts group: name or **Resume** (`automation-setup-draft-resume-<draft-id>`) and the pencil (**Edit**, `automation-setup-draft-edit-<draft-id>`) open `?draftId=<id>`.
- Kebab **Edit** on a dashboard card or the detail page header: edit mode (`?automationId=<id>`, `F21.edit`, `F23.edit-open`).
- A direct URL with `draftId` or `automationId` (see the cold-load gotcha).
families.given:
Preconditions:

- Baseline state (`launch`, `doctor`, `onboard --skip`). No LLM is needed: every bullet uses the Custom Python kind or never dispatches, and the agent-assisted path stays in F22.
- Desktop viewport; the `F28.error-contrast` bullet switches color themes (Settings → Application, `F16`) and restores the default.
- Every recipe below was run as written on 2026-10-15 on a fresh local `control-openhands launch` of main with Agent Server 1.54.0 and no LLM. Documented known failures remain failures.
families.gotchas:
- A toast can cover the toolbar (Save draft, Test, Close) and stays while the pointer rests on it, so the next toolbar click times out ("subtree intercepts pointer events"). After each save, `browser hover` a form field (for example `testid=automation-setup-name`) before clicking the toolbar again, as F22's Gotchas say.
- Drive inputs with `browser fill`: setting `.value` from `browser eval` does not reach React state for every field, and a save then sends the old value.
- Change one field per Save draft when checking a validation message: a save shows only the first server error, so two edits in one save hide the second.
- A cold load of `/automations/setup?draftId=<id>` or `?automationId=<id>` (a reload or a typed URL) opens the form: re-checked 2026-10-14 on a `control-openhands launch` of main with this family (both read their Name back). An earlier instance of unknown build stayed on **Loading saved draft…** for more than 20 s; if that returns, compare with opening the same draft from the dashboard.
- The draft bar duplicates the prompt error: `Field required` appears both under Prompt and in the bar.
- Kebab **Edit** on a Custom Python automation shows the code editor instead of the saved bundle summary: open bug #18341 (`F23`), with fixes in PRs #18353 and #18444.
- Escape on the setup page does nothing, by design (`F23.edit-close`).

features.description: Create Automation opens `/automations/setup` with Name pre-filled **New Automation** (placeholder `Standup digest`), an empty Prompt, Schedule selected with Daily at `09:00` in `America/New_York` (the default, whatever the browser's time zone), the docked composer (`Need help creating an automation?`) and no new conversation. The save state already reads **Unsaved changes** and the toolbar **Test** is disabled.

the button beside the Prompt label switches between Prompt and **Custom** (Custom Python). Custom shows a generated Python script that calls `AUTOMATION_CALLBACK_URL`, and **Entrypoint and setup** reveals Entrypoint `python3 main.py`, Setup script path `setup.sh` and a no-op setup script; switching back shows the Prompt again.

in create mode the Frequency control (the same control as on the edit page, whose presets and saving F23 owns as edit-schedule and edit-cron) starts on Daily at `09:00`, and switching presets fills create-mode defaults: Once a date-time at the next whole hour today, Weekly Monday, and Custom the cron of the preset it replaces (from Weekly, Monday at `10:30` it reads `30 10 * * 1`), while a cron already typed in Custom stays. Known failure (reproduced 2026-10-15, [#18461](https://github.com/OpenHands/OpenHands/issues/18461)): Custom shows the last custom cron, `0 9 * * *` until one is typed, whatever the preset; from Weekly on Monday it reads `0 9 * * *`. Every preset keeps the 13-entry time zone select.

choosing **Event** replaces the schedule with Event source (default **GitHub**, sent as `github`; its menu lists the webhook sources registered on this backend plus **Custom**), Event key (default `issue_comment.created`), **Add Filter** (one free-text filter input), **Ask Agent**, the notice `Event sources need a public URL to deliver webhooks to this instance.`, and a **Test event payload** pre-filled with a JSON object for that source and key. A source the backend has not registered (menu **Custom**, then a typed name) adds **Register this as a custom webhook source**, checked by default.
**Add Timeout** adds an optional **Timeout seconds** number field with a remove button; `1800` saves and the draft reads **Ready to test**.

**Save draft** works on any form, valid or not; the first save replaces the URL with `?draftId=<id>`, shows the **Draft saved** bar (relative time, **View test runs**, **Test**) and the toast `Draft saved in this conversation.`, and the save state reads **Saved just now**. The draft appears in the dashboard Drafts group (F21).

the server validates on save, not on blur. An invalid draft is still saved (`dispatchable: false`) and its first error replaces **Ready to test** in the draft bar: an empty prompt shows `Field required` (also under Prompt), a bad custom cron shows `Value error, Invalid cron expression: every day`. A field error stays until the next save. **Test** stays enabled on a saved invalid draft: it saves again, opens **Test runs** with the same error in a red alert and dispatches nothing.

a draft the server refuses outright (a timeout above 1800 returns `422`) sets the save state to **Save failed** and shows one error toast with the reason the API gives (a timeout of 1801 reads `Value error, timeout must not exceed 1800 seconds (30 minutes)`). The draft bar drops its validity pill (no stale **Ready to test**) until a save succeeds.

Test and Create check locally first and send nothing when a required field is empty: `Add a prompt before continuing.` (Prompt or Plugin kind), `Add a plugin source before continuing.`, `Add Python code before continuing.`, `Add an entrypoint command before continuing.`, `Add a setup script path before continuing.`, `Add a setup script before continuing.`; an event Test with a payload that is not a JSON object shows `Enter a valid JSON object before testing this event automation.` A blank Name is not an error: it is derived from the prompt.
in create mode **Test** stays disabled until the draft is saved and unchanged since; editing any field after a save disables it again until the next **Save draft**.

**Test** on a saved, valid draft opens **Test runs** (with **Back**), shows `Test run started.` and a Pending row; it runs a hidden disabled copy of the draft, not a dashboard automation. Expected: the row reaches Successful or Failed by itself. Known failure #18263 (reproduced again 2026-10-15 on a Custom Python draft): the row stays Pending and the page does not poll the runs after the first request.
**Create Automation** creates the automation enabled, navigates to `/automations/<id>` (a Custom Python automation shows **Script**), and removes the draft from the dashboard Drafts group.

the draft bar's error pill and the Test runs error alert use the theme's error color (`text-feedback-error`) and reach at least 4.5:1 in all five color themes. The pill uses a 5% red tint over the draft bar surface.
